Toolbox: Raster analysis\nDescription: A:
Tool: Aspect
Algorithm ID: gdal:aspect
Description: Generates an aspect map from any GDAL-supported elevation raster.
Aspect is the compass direction that a slope faces. The pixels will
have a value from 0-360° measured in degrees from north indicating the
azimuth.
On the northern hemisphere, the north side of slopes is often shaded
(small azimuth from 0°-90°), while the southern side receives more
solar radiation (higher azimuth from 180°-270°).
This algorithm is derived from the
`GDAL DEM utility <https://gdal.org/programs/gdaldem.html>`_.
**Default menu**: :menuselection:`Raster --> Analysis`
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: Input elevation raster layer (Type: str)
  - BAND: The number of the band to use as elevation (Type: str) [Default: 1]
  - TRIG_ANGLE: Activating the trigonometric angle results in different categories: 0° (East), 90° (North), 180° (West), 270° (South). (Type: bool) [Default: False]
  - ZERO_FLAT: Activating this option will insert a 0-value for the value -9999 on flat areas. (Type: bool) [Default: False]
  - COMPUTE_EDGES: Generates edges from the elevation raster (Type: bool) [Default: False]
  - ZEVENBERGEN: Activates Zevenbergen&Thorne formula for smooth landscapes (Type: bool) [Default: False]
  - OUTPUT: Output raster layer. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **file_output_types** :end-before: **end_file_output_types** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Save to temporary file]``]

Tool: Color relief
Algorithm ID: gdal:colorrelief
Description: Generates a color relief map from any GDAL-supported elevation raster.
Color reliefs can particularly be used to depict elevations.
The Algorithm outputs a 4-band raster with values computed from the
elevation and a text-based color configuration file.
By default, the colors between the given elevation values are blended
smoothly and the result is a nice colorized elevation raster.
This algorithm is derived from the
`GDAL DEM utility <https://gdal.org/programs/gdaldem.html>`_.
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: Input elevation raster layer (Type: str)
  - BAND: The number of the band to use as elevation (Type: str) [Default: 1]
  - COMPUTE_EDGES: Generates edges from the elevation raster (Type: bool) [Default: False]
  - COLOR_TABLE: A text-based color configuration file (Type: str)
  - MATCH_MODE: One of: * 0 --- Use strict color matching * 1 --- Use closest RGBA quadruples * 2 --- Use smoothly blended colours (Type: enum) [Default: 2]
  - OUTPUT: Output raster layer. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **file_output_types** :end-before: **end_file_output_types** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Save to temporary file]``]

Tool: Fill NoData
Algorithm ID: gdal:fillnodata
Description: Fill raster regions with NoData values by interpolation from edges.
The values for the NoData regions are calculated by the surrounding
pixel values using inverse distance weighting.
After the interpolation a smoothing of the results takes place.
Input can be any GDAL-supported raster layer. This algorithm is
generally suitable for interpolating missing regions of fairly
continuously varying rasters (such as elevation models for instance).
It is also suitable for filling small holes and cracks in more
irregularly varying images (like airphotos).
It is generally not so great for interpolating a raster from sparse
point data.
This algorithm is derived from the
`GDAL fillnodata utility <https://gdal.org/programs/gdal_fillnodata.html>`_.
**Default menu**: :menuselection:`Raster --> Analysis`
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: Input raster layer (Type: str)
  - BAND: The band to operate on. NoData values must be represented by the value 0. (Type: str) [Default: 1]
  - DISTANCE: The number of pixels to search in all directions to find values to interpolate from (Type: int) [Default: 10]
  - ITERATIONS: The number of 3x3 filter passes to run (0 or more) to smoothen the results of the interpolation. (Type: int) [Default: 0]
  - NO_MASK: Activates the user-defined validity mask (Type: bool) [Default: False]
  - MASK_LAYER: A raster layer that defines the areas to fill. (Type: str)
  - OUTPUT: Specification of the output raster layer. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **file_output_types** :end-before: **end_file_output_types** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Save to temporary file]``]

Tool: Grid (Data metrics)
Algorithm ID: gdal:griddatametrics
Description: Computes some data metrics using the specified window and output grid
geometry.
This algorithm is derived from the
`GDAL grid utility <https://gdal.org/programs/gdal_grid.html>`_.
.. seealso:: `GDAL grid tutorial <https://gdal.org/tutorials/gdal_grid_tut.html>`_
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: Input point vector layer (Type: str)
  - METRIC: One of: * 0 --- Minimum, minimum value found in grid node search ellipse * 1 --- Maximum, maximum value found in grid node search ellipse * 2 --- Range, a difference between the minimum and maximum values found in grid node search ellipse * 3 --- Count, a number of data points found in grid node search ellipse * 4 --- Average distance, an average distance between the grid node (center of the search ellipse) and all of the data points found in grid node search ellipse * 5 --- Average distance between points, an average distance between the data points found in grid node search ellipse. The distance between each pair of points within ellipse is calculated and average of all distances is set as a grid node value (Type: enum) [Default: 0]
  - RADIUS_1: The first radius (X axis if rotation angle is 0) of the search ellipse (Type: float) [Default: 0.0]
  - RADIUS_2: The second radius (Y axis if rotation angle is 0) of the search ellipse (Type: float) [Default: 0.0]
  - ANGLE: Angle of ellipse rotation in degrees. Ellipse rotated counter clockwise. (Type: float) [Default: 0.0]
  - MIN_POINTS: Minimum number of data points to average. If less amount of points found the grid node considered empty and will be filled with NoData marker. (Type: float) [Default: 0.0]
  - NODATA: NoData marker to fill empty points (Type: float) [Default: 0.0]
  - OUTPUT: Specify the output raster layer with interpolated values. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **file_output_types** :end-before: **end_file_output_types** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Save to temporary file]``]
Advanced Parameters:
  - DATA_TYPE: Defines the data type of the output raster file. Options: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **raster_data_types** :end-before: **end_raster_data_types** (Type: enum) [Default: 5]

Tool: Grid (IDW with nearest neighbor searching)
Algorithm ID: gdal:gridinversedistancenearestneighbor
Description: Computes the Inverse Distance to a Power gridding combined to the
nearest neighbor method.
Ideal when a maximum number of data points to use is required.
This algorithm is derived from the
`GDAL grid utility <https://gdal.org/programs/gdal_grid.html>`_.
.. seealso:: `GDAL grid tutorial <https://gdal.org/tutorials/gdal_grid_tut.html>`_
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: Input point vector layer (Type: str)
  - POWER: Weighting power (Type: float) [Default: 2.0]
  - SMOOTHING: Smoothing parameter (Type: float) [Default: 0.0]
  - RADIUS: The radius of the search circle (Type: float) [Default: 1.0]
  - MAX_POINTS: Do not search for more points than this number. (Type: int) [Default: 12]
  - MIN_POINTS: Minimum number of data points to average. If less amount of points found the grid node considered empty and will be filled with NoData marker. (Type: int) [Default: 0]
  - NODATA: NoData marker to fill empty points (Type: float) [Default: 0.0]
  - OUTPUT: Specify the output raster layer with interpolated values. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **file_output_types** :end-before: **end_file_output_types** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Save to temporary file]``]
Advanced Parameters:
  - DATA_TYPE: Defines the data type of the output raster file. Options: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **raster_data_types** :end-before: **end_raster_data_types** (Type: enum) [Default: 5]

Tool: Grid (Inverse distance to a power)
Algorithm ID: gdal:gridinversedistance
Description: The Inverse Distance to a Power gridding method is a weighted average
interpolator.
You should supply the input arrays with the scattered data values
including coordinates of every data point and output grid geometry.
The function will compute interpolated value for the given position in output grid.
This algorithm is derived from the
`GDAL grid utility <https://gdal.org/programs/gdal_grid.html>`_.
.. seealso:: `GDAL grid tutorial <https://gdal.org/tutorials/gdal_grid_tut.html>`_
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: Input point vector layer (Type: str)
  - POWER: Weighting power (Type: float) [Default: 2.0]
  - SMOOTHING: Smoothing parameter (Type: float) [Default: 0.0]
  - RADIUS_1: The first radius (X axis if rotation angle is 0) of the search ellipse (Type: float) [Default: 0.0]
  - RADIUS_2: The second radius (Y axis if rotation angle is 0) of the search ellipse (Type: float) [Default: 0.0]
  - ANGLE: Angle of ellipse rotation in degrees. Ellipse rotated counter clockwise. (Type: float) [Default: 0.0]
  - MAX_POINTS: Do not search for more points than this number. (Type: int) [Default: 0]
  - MIN_POINTS: Minimum number of data points to average. If less amount of points found the grid node considered empty and will be filled with NoData marker. (Type: int) [Default: 0]
  - NODATA: NoData marker to fill empty points (Type: float) [Default: 0.0]
  - OUTPUT: Specify the output raster layer with interpolated values. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **file_output_types** :end-before: **end_file_output_types** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Save to temporary file]``]
Advanced Parameters:
  - DATA_TYPE: Defines the data type of the output raster file. Options: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **raster_data_types** :end-before: **end_raster_data_types** (Type: enum) [Default: 5]

Tool: Grid (Linear)
Algorithm ID: gdal:gridlinear
Description: The Linear method perform linear interpolation by computing a Delaunay
triangulation of the point cloud, finding in which triangle of the
triangulation the point is, and by doing linear interpolation from its
barycentric coordinates within the triangle.
If the point is not in any triangle, depending on the radius, the
algorithm will use the value of the nearest point or the NoData value.
This algorithm is derived from the
`GDAL grid utility <https://gdal.org/programs/gdal_grid.html>`_.
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: Input point vector layer (Type: str)
  - RADIUS: In case the point to be interpolated does not fit into a triangle of the Delaunay triangulation, use that maximum distance to search a nearest neighbour, or use NoData otherwise. If set to ``-1``, the search distance is infinite. If set to ``0``, NoData value will be used. (Type: float) [Default: -1.0]
  - NODATA: NoData marker to fill empty points (Type: float) [Default: 0.0]
  - OUTPUT: Specify the output raster layer with interpolated values. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **file_output_types** :end-before: **end_file_output_types** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Save to temporary file]``]
Advanced Parameters:
  - DATA_TYPE: Defines the data type of the output raster file. Options: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **raster_data_types** :end-before: **end_raster_data_types** (Type: enum) [Default: 5]

Tool: Grid (Moving average)
Algorithm ID: gdal:gridaverage
Description: The Moving Average is a simple data averaging algorithm.
It uses a moving window of elliptic form to search values and averages
all data points within the window.
Search ellipse can be rotated by specified angle, the center of
ellipse located at the grid node.
Also the minimum number of data points to average can be set, if there
are not enough points in window, the grid node considered empty and
will be filled with specified NoData value.
This algorithm is derived from the
`GDAL grid utility <https://gdal.org/programs/gdal_grid.html>`_.
.. seealso:: `GDAL grid tutorial <https://gdal.org/tutorials/gdal_grid_tut.html>`_
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: Input point vector layer (Type: str)
  - RADIUS_1: The first radius (X axis if rotation angle is 0) of the search ellipse (Type: float) [Default: 0.0]
  - RADIUS_2: The second radius (Y axis if rotation angle is 0) of the search ellipse (Type: float) [Default: 0.0]
  - ANGLE: Angle of ellipse rotation in degrees. Ellipse rotated counter clockwise. (Type: float) [Default: 0.0]
  - MIN_POINTS: Minimum number of data points to average. If less amount of points found the grid node considered empty and will be filled with NoData marker. (Type: float) [Default: 0.0]
  - NODATA: NoData marker to fill empty points (Type: float) [Default: 0.0]
  - OUTPUT: Specify the output raster layer. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **file_output_types** :end-before: **end_file_output_types** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Save to temporary file]``]
Advanced Parameters:
  - DATA_TYPE: Defines the data type of the output raster file. Options: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **raster_data_types** :end-before: **end_raster_data_types** (Type: enum) [Default: 5]

Tool: Grid (Nearest neighbor)
Algorithm ID: gdal:gridnearestneighbor
Description: The Nearest Neighbor method doesn't perform any interpolation or
smoothing, it just takes the value of nearest point found in grid node
search ellipse and returns it as a result.
If there are no points found, the specified NoData value will be
returned.
This algorithm is derived from the
`GDAL grid utility <https://gdal.org/programs/gdal_grid.html>`_.
.. seealso:: `GDAL grid tutorial <https://gdal.org/tutorials/gdal_grid_tut.html>`_
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: Input point vector layer (Type: str)
  - RADIUS_1: The first radius (X axis if rotation angle is 0) of the search ellipse (Type: float) [Default: 0.0]
  - RADIUS_2: The second radius (Y axis if rotation angle is 0) of the search ellipse (Type: float) [Default: 0.0]
  - ANGLE: Angle of ellipse rotation in degrees. Ellipse rotated counter clockwise. (Type: float) [Default: 0.0]
  - NODATA: NoData marker to fill empty points (Type: float) [Default: 0.0]
  - OUTPUT: Specify the output raster layer with interpolated values. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **file_output_types** :end-before: **end_file_output_types** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Save to temporary file]``]
Advanced Parameters:
  - DATA_TYPE: Defines the data type of the output raster file. Options: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **raster_data_types** :end-before: **end_raster_data_types** (Type: enum) [Default: 5]

Tool: Hillshade
Algorithm ID: gdal:hillshade
Description: Outputs a raster with a nice shaded relief effect.
It’s very useful for visualizing the terrain.
You can optionally specify the azimuth and altitude of the light
source, a vertical exaggeration factor and a scaling factor to account
for differences between vertical and horizontal units.
This algorithm is derived from the
`GDAL DEM utility <https://gdal.org/programs/gdaldem.html>`__ .
**Default menu**: :menuselection:`Raster --> Analysis`
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: Input Elevation raster layer (Type: str)
  - BAND: Band containing the elevation information (Type: str) [Default: 1]
  - Z_FACTOR: The factor exaggerates the height of the output elevation raster (Type: float) [Default: 1.0]
  - SCALE: The ratio of vertical units to horizontal units (Type: float) [Default: 1.0]
  - AZIMUTH: Defines the azimuth of the light shining on the elevation raster in degrees. If it comes from the top of the raster the value is 0, if it comes from the east it is 90 a.s.o. (Type: float) [Default: 315.0]
  - ALTITUDE: Defines the altitude of the light, in degrees. 90 if the light comes from above the elevation raster, 0 if it is raking light. (Type: float) [Default: 45.0]
  - COMPUTE_EDGES: Generates edges from the elevation raster (Type: bool) [Default: False]
  - ZEVENBERGEN: Activates Zevenbergen&Thorne formula for smooth landscapes (Type: bool) [Default: False]
  - COMBINED: - (Type: bool) [Default: False]
  - MULTIDIRECTIONAL: - (Type: bool) [Default: False]
  - OUTPUT: Specify the output raster layer with interpolated values. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **file_output_types** :end-before: **end_file_output_types** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Save to temporary file]``]

Tool: Near black
Algorithm ID: gdal:nearblack
Description: Converts nearly black/white borders to black.
This algorithm will scan an image and try to set all pixels that are
nearly or exactly black, white or one or more custom colors around the
collar to black or white.
This is often used to "fix up" lossy compressed airphotos so that
color pixels can be treated as transparent when mosaicking.
This algorithm is derived from the
`GDAL nearblack utility <https://gdal.org/programs/nearblack.html>`_.
**Default menu**: :menuselection:`Raster --> Analysis`
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: Input Elevation raster layer (Type: str)
  - NEAR: Select how far from black, white or custom colors the pixel values can be and still considered near black, white or custom color. (Type: int) [Default: 15]
  - WHITE: Search for nearly white (255) pixels instead of nearly black pixels (Type: bool) [Default: False]
  - OUTPUT: Specify the output raster layer. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **file_output_types** :end-before: **end_file_output_types** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Save to temporary file]``]

Tool: Proximity (raster distance)
Algorithm ID: gdal:proximity
Description: Generates a raster proximity map indicating the distance from the
center of each pixel to the center of the nearest pixel identified as
a target pixel.
Target pixels are those in the source raster for which the raster
pixel value is in the set of target pixel values.
This algorithm is derived from the
`GDAL proximity utility <https://gdal.org/programs/gdal_proximity.html>`_.
**Default menu**: :menuselection:`Raster --> Analysis`
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: Input Elevation raster layer (Type: str)
  - BAND: Band containing the elevation information (Type: str) [Default: 1]
  - UNITS: Indicate whether distances generated should be in pixel or georeferenced coordinates. One of: * 0 --- Georeferenced coordinates * 1 --- Pixel coordinates (Type: enum) [Default: 1]
  - OUTPUT: Specify the output raster layer. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **file_output_types** :end-before: **end_file_output_types** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Save to temporary file]``]
Advanced Parameters:
  - DATA_TYPE: Defines the data type of the output raster file. Options: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **raster_data_types** :end-before: **end_raster_data_types** (Type: enum) [Default: 5]

Tool: Roughness
Algorithm ID: gdal:roughness
Description: Outputs a single-band raster with values computed from the elevation.
Roughness is the degree of irregularity of the surface.
It's calculated by the largest inter-cell difference of a central
pixel and its surrounding cell.
The determination of the roughness plays a role in the analysis of
terrain elevation data, it's useful for calculations of the river
morphology, in climatology and physical geography in general.
This algorithm is derived from the
`GDAL DEM utility <https://gdal.org/programs/gdaldem.html>`_.
**Default menu**: :menuselection:`Raster --> Analysis`
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: Input elevation raster layer (Type: str)
  - BAND: The number of the band to use as elevation (Type: str) [Default: 1]
  - COMPUTE_EDGES: Generates edges from the elevation raster (Type: bool) [Default: False]
  - OUTPUT: Specify the output raster layer. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **file_output_types** :end-before: **end_file_output_types** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Save to temporary file]``]

Tool: Sieve
Algorithm ID: gdal:sieve
Description: Removes raster polygons smaller than a provided threshold size (in
pixels) and replaces them with the pixel value of the largest
neighbour polygon.
It is useful if you have a large amount of small areas on your raster
map.
This algorithm is derived from the
`GDAL sieve utility <https://gdal.org/programs/gdal_sieve.html>`_.
**Default menu**: :menuselection:`Raster --> Analysis`
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: Input elevation raster layer (Type: str)
  - THRESHOLD: Only raster polygons smaller than this size will be removed (Type: int) [Default: 10]
  - EIGHT_CONNECTEDNESS: Use eight connectedness instead of four connectedness (Type: bool) [Default: False]
  - NO_MASK: - (Type: bool) [Default: False]
  - OUTPUT: Specify the output raster layer. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **file_output_types** :end-before: **end_file_output_types** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Save to temporary file]``]

Tool: Slope
Algorithm ID: gdal:slope
Description: Generates a slope map from any GDAL-supported elevation raster.
Slope is the angle of inclination to the horizontal. 
You have the option of specifying the type of slope value you want:
degrees or percent slope.
This algorithm is derived from the
`GDAL DEM utility <https://gdal.org/programs/gdaldem.html>`_.
**Default menu**: :menuselection:`Raster --> Analysis`
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: Input Elevation raster layer (Type: str)
  - BAND: Band containing the elevation information (Type: str) [Default: 1]
  - SCALE: The ratio of vertical units to horizontal units (Type: float) [Default: 1.0]
  - AS_PERCENT: Express slope as percent instead of degrees (Type: bool) [Default: False]
  - COMPUTE_EDGES: Generates edges from the elevation raster (Type: bool) [Default: False]
  - ZEVENBERGEN: Activates Zevenbergen&Thorne formula for smooth landscapes (Type: bool) [Default: False]
  - OUTPUT: Specify the output raster layer. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **file_output_types** :end-before: **end_file_output_types** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Save to temporary file]``]

Tool: Terrain Ruggedness Index (TRI)
Algorithm ID: gdal:triterrainruggednessindex
Description: Outputs a single-band raster with values computed from the
elevation.
TRI stands for Terrain Ruggedness Index, which is defined
as the mean difference between a central pixel and its
surrounding cells.
This algorithm is derived from the
`GDAL DEM utility <https://gdal.org/programs/gdaldem.html>`_.
**Default menu**: :menuselection:`Raster --> Analysis`
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: Input elevation raster layer (Type: str)
  - BAND: The number of the band to use as elevation (Type: str) [Default: 1]
  - COMPUTE_EDGES: Generates edges from the elevation raster (Type: bool) [Default: False]
  - OUTPUT: Specify the output raster layer. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **file_output_types** :end-before: **end_file_output_types** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Save to temporary file]``]

Tool: Topographic Position Index (TPI)
Algorithm ID: gdal:tpitopographicpositionindex
Description: Outputs a single-band raster with values computed from the elevation.
TPI stands for Topographic Position Index, which is defined as the
difference between a central pixel and the mean of its surrounding
cells.
This algorithm is derived from the
`GDAL DEM utility <https://gdal.org/programs/gdaldem.html>`_.
**Default menu**: :menuselection:`Raster --> Analysis`
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: Input elevation raster layer (Type: str)
  - BAND: The number of the band to use for elevation values (Type: str) [Default: 1]
  - COMPUTE_EDGES: Generates edges from the elevation raster (Type: bool) [Default: False]
  - OUTPUT: Specify the output raster layer. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **file_output_types** :end-before: **end_file_output_types** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Save to temporary file]``]
Toolbox: Raster conversion\nDescription::
Tool: gdal2xyz
Algorithm ID: gdal:gdal2xyz
Description: Converts raster data to XYZ ASCII file format.
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: Raster layer to convert (Type: str)
  - BAND: If the raster is multiband, choose the band you want to convert (Type: str) [Default: The first band of the input layer]
  - SKIP_NODATA: Do not output "NoData" values (GDAL >= 3.3). (Type: bool) [Default: False]
  - CSV: Sets whether the output file should be of type comma-separated values (csv). (Type: bool) [Default: False]
  - OUTPUT: Specification of the output file. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **file_output_types** :end-before: **end_file_output_types** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Save to temporary file]``]

Tool: PCT to RGB
Algorithm ID: gdal:pcttorgb
Description: Converts an 8 bit paletted image to a 24 bit RGB.
It will convert a pseudocolor band from the input file to
an RGB file of the desired format.
This algorithm is derived from the
`GDAL pct2rgb utility <https://gdal.org/programs/pct2rgb.html>`_.
**Default menu**: :menuselection:`Raster --> Conversion`
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: Input 8 bit raster image (Type: str)
  - BAND: If the raster is multiband, choose the band you want to convert (Type: str) [Default: The first band of the input layer]
  - RGBA: Sets whether the output file should be of type RGBA. (Type: bool) [Default: False]
  - OUTPUT: Specification of the output file. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **file_output_types** :end-before: **end_file_output_types** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Save to temporary file]``]

Tool: Polygonize (raster to vector)
Algorithm ID: gdal:polygonize
Description: Creates vector polygons for all connected regions of pixels in the
raster sharing a common pixel value. Each polygon is created with an
attribute indicating the pixel value of that polygon.
This algorithm is derived from the
`GDAL polygonize utility <https://gdal.org/programs/gdal_polygonize.html>`_.
**Default menu**: :menuselection:`Raster --> Conversion`
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: Input raster layer (Type: str)
  - BAND: If the raster is multiband, choose the band you want to use (Type: str) [Default: The first band of the input layer]
  - FIELD: Specify the field name for the attributes of the connected regions. (Type: str) [Default: 'DN']
  - EIGHT_CONNECTEDNESS: If not set, raster cells must have a common border to be considered connected (*4-connected*). If set, touching raster cells are also considered connected (*8-connected*). (Type: bool) [Default: False]
  - OUTPUT: Specification of the output (polygon) vector layer. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **file_output_types** :end-before: **end_file_output_types** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Save to temporary file]``]

Tool: Rearrange bands
Algorithm ID: gdal:rearrange_bands
Description: Creates a new raster using selected band(s) from a given raster layer.
The algorithm also makes it possible to reorder the bands for the
newly-created raster.
This algorithm is derived from the
`GDAL translate utility <https://gdal.org/programs/gdal_translate.html>`_.
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: Input raster layer (Type: str)
  - BANDS: Ordered list of the bands to use to create the new raster (Type: list) [Default: None]
  - OUTPUT: Specification of the output raster. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **file_output_types** :end-before: **end_file_output_types** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Save to temporary file]``]
Advanced Parameters:
  - DATA_TYPE: Defines the data type of the output raster file. Options: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **raster_data_types_extended** :end-before: **end_raster_data_types_extended** (Type: enum) [Default: 0]

Tool: RGB to PCT
Algorithm ID: gdal:rgbtopct
Description: Converts a 24 bit RGB image into a 8 bit paletted.
Computes an optimal pseudo-color table for the given RGB-image using a
median cut algorithm on a downsampled RGB histogram.
Then it converts the image into a pseudo-colored image using the color
table. This conversion utilizes Floyd-Steinberg dithering (error
diffusion) to maximize output image visual quality.
If you want to classify a raster map and want to reduce the number of
classes it can be helpful to downsample your image with this algorithm
before.
This algorithm is derived from the
`GDAL rgb2pct utility <https://gdal.org/programs/rgb2pct.html>`_.
**Default menu**: :menuselection:`Raster --> Conversion`
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: Input (RGB) raster layer (Type: str)
  - NCOLORS: The number of colors the resulting image will contain. A value from 2-256 is possible. (Type: int) [Default: 2]
  - OUTPUT: Specification of the output raster. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **file_output_types** :end-before: **end_file_output_types** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Save to temporary file]``]

Tool: Translate (convert format)
Algorithm ID: gdal:translate
Description: Converts raster data between different formats.
This algorithm is derived from the
`GDAL translate utility <https://gdal.org/programs/gdal_translate.html>`_.
**Default menu**: :menuselection:`Raster --> Conversion`
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: Input raster layer (Type: str)
  - COPY_SUBDATASETS: Create individual files for subdatasets (Type: bool) [Default: False]
  - OUTPUT: Specification of the output (translated) raster layer. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **file_output_types** :end-before: **end_file_output_types** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Save to temporary file]``]
Advanced Parameters:
  - DATA_TYPE: Defines the data type of the output raster file. Options: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **raster_data_types_extended** :end-before: **end_raster_data_types_extended** (Type: enum) [Default: 0]
Toolbox: Raster extraction\nDescription::
Tool: Clip raster by extent
Algorithm ID: gdal:cliprasterbyextent
Description: Clips any GDAL-supported raster file to a given extent.
This algorithm is derived from the
`GDAL translate utility <https://gdal.org/programs/gdal_translate.html>`_.
**Default menu**: :menuselection:`Raster --> Extraction`
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: The input raster (Type: str)
  - EXTENT: Extent that should be used for the output raster. Only pixels within the specified bounding box will be included in the output. .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **extent_options** :end-before: **end_extent_options** (Type: str)
  - OVERCRS: If checked, the output file is assigned the input layer CRS. (Type: bool) [Default: False]
  - OUTPUT: Specification of the output raster layer. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **file_output_types** :end-before: **end_file_output_types** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Save to temporary file]``]
Advanced Parameters:
  - DATA_TYPE: Defines the format of the output raster file. Options: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **raster_data_types_extended** :end-before: **end_raster_data_types_extended** (Type: enum) [Default: 0]

Tool: Clip raster by mask layer
Algorithm ID: gdal:cliprasterbymasklayer
Description: Clips any GDAL-supported raster by a vector mask layer.
This algorithm is derived from the
`GDAL warp utility <https://gdal.org/programs/gdalwarp.html>`_.
**Default menu**: :menuselection:`Raster --> Extraction`
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: The input raster (Type: str)
  - MASK: Vector mask for clipping the raster (Type: str)
  - SOURCE_CRS: Set the coordinate reference to use for the input raster (Type: str)
  - TARGET_CRS: Set the coordinate reference to use for the mask layer (Type: str)
  - ALPHA_BAND: Creates an alpha band for the result. The alpha band then includes the transparency values of the pixels. (Type: bool) [Default: False]
  - CROP_TO_CUTLINE: Applies the vector layer extent to the output raster if checked. (Type: bool) [Default: True]
  - KEEP_RESOLUTION: The resolution of the output raster will not be changed (Type: bool) [Default: False]
  - SET_RESOLUTION: Shall the output resolution (cell size) be specified (Type: bool) [Default: False]
  - MULTITHREADING: Two threads will be used to process chunks of image and perform input/output operation simultaneously. Note that computation is not multithreaded itself. (Type: bool) [Default: False]
  - OUTPUT: Specification of the output raster layer. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **file_output_types** :end-before: **end_file_output_types** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Save to temporary file]``]
Advanced Parameters:
  - DATA_TYPE: Defines the format of the output raster file. Options: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **raster_data_types_extended** :end-before: **end_raster_data_types_extended** (Type: enum) [Default: 0]

Tool: Contour
Algorithm ID: gdal:contour
Description: Extracts contour lines from any GDAL-supported elevation raster.
This algorithm is derived from the
`GDAL contour utility <https://gdal.org/programs/gdal_contour.html>`_.
**Default menu**: :menuselection:`Raster --> Extraction`
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: Input raster (Type: str)
  - BAND: Raster band to create the contours from (Type: str) [Default: 1]
  - INTERVAL: Defines the interval between the contour lines in the given units of the elevation raster (minimum value 0) (Type: float) [Default: 10.0]
  - OUTPUT: Specification of the output vector layer. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **file_output_types** :end-before: **end_file_output_types** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Save to temporary file]``]
Advanced Parameters:
  - CREATE_3D: Forces production of 3D vectors instead of 2D. Includes elevation at every vertex. (Type: bool) [Default: False]
  - IGNORE_NODATA: Ignores any NoData values in the dataset. (Type: bool) [Default: False]

Tool: Contour Polygons
Algorithm ID: gdal:contour_polygon
Description: Extracts contour polygons from any GDAL-supported elevation raster.
This algorithm is derived from the
`GDAL contour utility <https://gdal.org/programs/gdal_contour.html>`_.
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: Input raster (Type: str)
  - BAND: Raster band to create the contours from (Type: str) [Default: 1]
  - INTERVAL: Defines the interval between the contour lines in the given units of the elevation raster (minimum value 0) (Type: float) [Default: 10.0]
  - OUTPUT: Specification of the output vector layer. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **file_output_types** :end-before: **end_file_output_types** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Save to temporary file]``]
Advanced Parameters:
  - CREATE_3D: Forces production of 3D vectors instead of 2D. Includes elevation at every vertex. (Type: bool) [Default: False]
  - IGNORE_NODATA: Ignores any NoData values in the dataset. (Type: bool) [Default: False]
Toolbox: Raster miscellaneous\nDescripti:
Tool: Build overviews (pyramids)
Algorithm ID: gdal:overviews
Description: To speed up rendering time of raster layers overviews (pyramids) can
be created. Overviews are lower resolution copies of the data which
QGIS uses depending of the level of zoom.
This algorithm is derived from the
`GDAL addo utility <https://gdal.org/programs/gdaladdo.html>`_.
**Default menu**: :menuselection:`Raster --> Miscellaneous`
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: Input raster layer (Type: str)
  - CLEAN: Removes existing overviews from the raster. By default these are not removed. (Type: bool) [Default: False]
Advanced Parameters:
  - LEVELS: Defines the number of overview levels calculated by the original resolution of the input raster layer. By default 4 levels will be taken into consideration. (Type: str) [Default: '2 4 8 16']

Tool: Build virtual raster
Algorithm ID: gdal:buildvirtualraster
Description: Builds a VRT (Virtual Dataset) that is a mosaic of the list of input
GDAL-supported rasters.
With a mosaic you can merge several raster files.
This algorithm is derived from the
`GDAL buildvrt utility <https://gdal.org/programs/gdalbuildvrt.html>`_.
**Default menu**: :menuselection:`Raster --> Miscellaneous`
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: GDAL-supported raster layers. (Type: list)
  - RESOLUTION: The output resolution of the mosaic. By default the average resolution of the raster files will be chosen. Options: * 0 --- Average (``average``) * 1 --- Highest (``highest``) * 2 --- Lowest (``lowest``) (Type: enum) [Default: 0]
  - SEPARATE: With 'True' you can define that each raster file goes into a separated stacked band in the VRT band. (Type: bool) [Default: False]
  - PROJ_DIFFERENCE: Allows that the output bands have different projections derived from the projection of the input raster layers. (Type: bool) [Default: False]
  - OUTPUT: Specification of the output raster layer. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **file_output_types** :end-before: **end_file_output_types** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Save to temporary file]``]
Advanced Parameters:
  - ADD_ALPHA: Adds an alpha mask band to the VRT when the source raster has none. (Type: bool) [Default: False]
  - RESAMPLING: The `resampling algorithm <https://gdal.org/programs/gdalwarp.html#cmdoption-gdalwarp-r>`_ to use. Options: * 0 --- Nearest Neighbour (``nearest``) * 1 --- Bilinear (2x2 kernel) (``bilinear``) * 2 --- Cubic (4x4 kernel) (``cubic``) * 3 --- Cubic B-Spline (4x4 kernel) (``cubicspline``) * 4 --- Lanczos (6x6 kernel) (``lanczos``) * 5 --- Average (``average``) * 6 --- Mode (``mode``) (Type: enum) [Default: 0]
  - EXTRA: Add extra GDAL command line options (Type: str) [Default: None]

Tool: gdal2tiles
Algorithm ID: gdal:gdal2tiles
Description: Generates a directory with small tiles and metadata, following the
`OSGeo Tile Map Service Specification <https://wiki.osgeo.org/wiki/Tile_Map_Service_Specification>`_.
See also the
`OpenGIS Web Map Tile Service Implementation Standard
<https://www.ogc.org/standards/wmts>`_.
Simple web pages with viewers based on Google Maps, OpenLayers and
Leaflet are generated as well.
To explore your maps on-line in the web browser, you only need to
upload the generated directory onto a web server.
This algorithm also creates the necessary metadata for Google Earth
(KML SuperOverlay), in case the supplied map uses ``EPSG:4326``
projection.
ESRI world files and embedded georeferencing is used during tile
generation, but you can publish a picture without proper
georeferencing too.
This algorithm is derived from the
`GDAL gdal2tiles utility <https://gdal.org/programs/gdal2tiles.html>`_.
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: GDAL-supported raster layer. (Type: str)
  - PROFILE: One of: * 0 --- Mercator (``mercator``) * 1 --- Geodetic (``geodetic``) * 2 --- Raster (``raster``) (Type: enum) [Default: 0]
  - VIEWER: One of: * 0 --- All (``all``) * 1 --- GoogleMaps (``google``) * 2 --- OpenLayers (``openlayers``) * 3 --- Leaflet (``leaflet``) * 4 --- None (``none``) (Type: str) [Default: 0]
  - COPYRIGHT: - (Type: str) [Default: '']
  - OUTPUT: Specify the output folder for the tiles. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **directory_output_types** :end-before: **end_directory_output_types** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Save to temporary folder]``]
Advanced Parameters:
  - RESAMPLING: The resampling algorithm to use. Options: * 0 --- Average (``average``) * 1 --- Nearest Neighbour (``near``) * 2 --- Bilinear (2x2 kernel) (``bilinear``) * 3 --- Cubic (4x4 kernel) (``cubic``) * 4 --- Cubic B-Spline (4x4 kernel) (``cubicspline``) * 5 --- Lanczos (6x6 kernel) (``lanczos``) * 6 --- Antialias (``antialias``) (Type: enum) [Default: 0]
  - RESUME: - (Type: bool) [Default: False]
  - KML: - (Type: bool) [Default: False]
  - NO_KML: - (Type: bool) [Default: False]

Tool: Merge
Algorithm ID: gdal:merge
Description: Merges raster files in a simple way. Here you can use a pseudocolor
table from an input raster and define the output raster type. All
the images must be in the same coordinate system.
This algorithm is derived from the
`GDAL merge utility <https://gdal.org/programs/gdal_merge.html>`_.
**Default menu**: :menuselection:`Raster --> Miscellaneous`
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: Input raster layers (Type: list)
  - PCT: The pseudocolor table from the first layer will be used for the coloring (Type: bool) [Default: False]
  - SEPARATE: Place each input file into a separate band (Type: bool) [Default: False]
  - DATA_TYPE: Defines the format of the output raster file. Options: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **raster_data_types** :end-before: **end_raster_data_types** (Type: enum) [Default: 5]
  - OUTPUT: Specification of the output raster layer. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **file_output_types** :end-before: **end_file_output_types** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Save to temporary file]``]
Advanced Parameters:
  - EXTRA: Add extra GDAL command line options (Type: str) [Default: None]

Tool: Pansharpening
Algorithm ID: gdal:pansharp
Description: Performs a pan-sharpening operation.
It can create a "classic" output dataset (such as GeoTIFF),
or a VRT dataset describing the pan-sharpening operation.
See `GDAL Pansharpen <https://gdal.org/programs/gdal_pansharpen.html>`_.
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - SPECTRAL: Input (spectral) raster layer (Type: str)
  - PANCHROMATIC: Input (panchromatic) raster layer (Type: str)
  - OUTPUT: Specify the output (sharpened) raster layer. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **file_output_types** :end-before: **end_file_output_types** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Save to temporary file]``]
Advanced Parameters:
  - RESAMPLING: The `resampling algorithm <https://gdal.org/programs/gdalwarp.html#cmdoption-gdalwarp-r>`_ to use. Options: * 0 --- Nearest Neighbour (``nearest``) * 1 --- Bilinear (2x2 kernel) (``bilinear``) * 2 --- Cubic (4x4 kernel) (``cubic``) * 3 --- Cubic B-Spline (4x4 kernel) (``cubicspline``) * 4 --- Lanczos (6x6 kernel) (``lanczos``) * 5 --- Average (``average``) (Type: enum) [Default: 2]

Tool: Raster calculator
Algorithm ID: gdal:rastercalculator
Description: Command line raster calculator with numpy syntax.
Use any basic arithmetic supported by numpy arrays,
such as +, -, \*, and / along with logical operators,
such as >.
Note that all input rasters must have the same
dimensions, but no projection checking is performed.
See the
`GDAL Raster Calculator utility docs <https://gdal.org/programs/gdal_calc.html>`_.
.. seealso:: :ref:`qgisrastercalc`, :ref:`qgisvirtualrastercalc`
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT_A: First input raster layer (mandatory) (Type: str)
  - BAND_A: Band for input layer A (mandatory) (Type: str)

Tool: Raster information
Algorithm ID: gdal:gdalinfo
Description: The gdalinfo program lists various information about a GDAL supported
raster dataset.
This algorithm is derived from the
`GDAL info utility <https://gdal.org/programs/gdalinfo.html>`_.
**Default menu**: :menuselection:`Raster --> Miscellaneous`
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: Input raster layer (Type: str)
  - MIN_MAX: Forces computation of the actual min/max values for each band in the dataset (Type: bool) [Default: False]
  - STATS: Reads and displays image statistics. Forces computation if no statistics are stored in an image. (Type: bool) [Default: False]
  - NO_GCP: Suppresses ground control points list printing. It may be useful for datasets with huge amount of GCPs, such as L1B AVHRR or HDF4 MODIS which contain thousands of them. (Type: bool) [Default: False]
  - NO_METADATA: Suppresses metadata printing. Some datasets may contain a lot of metadata strings. (Type: bool) [Default: False]
  - OUTPUT: Specify the HTML file for output. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **file_output_types** :end-before: **end_file_output_types** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Save to temporary file]``]

Tool: Retile
Algorithm ID: gdal:retile
Description: Retiles a set of input tiles.
All the input tiles must be georeferenced in the same
coordinate system and have a matching number of bands.
Optionally pyramid levels are generated.
This algorithm is derived from the
`GDAL Retile utility <https://gdal.org/programs/gdal_retile.html>`_.
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: The input raster files (Type: list)
  - TILE_SIZE_X: Width of the tiles in pixels (minimum 0) (Type: int) [Default: 256]
  - TILE_SIZE_Y: Height of the tiles in pixels (minimum 0) (Type: int) [Default: 256]
  - OVERLAP: - (Type: int) [Default: 0]
  - LEVELS: Minimum: 0 (Type: int) [Default: 1]
  - OUTPUT: Specify the output folder for the tiles. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **directory_output_types** :end-before: **end_directory_output_types** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Save to temporary folder]``]
  - OUTPUT_CSV: Specify the output file for the tiles. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **file_output_types_skip** :end-before: **end_file_output_types_skip** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Skip output]``]
Advanced Parameters:
  - RESAMPLING: The `resampling algorithm <https://gdal.org/programs/gdalwarp.html#cmdoption-gdalwarp-r>`_ to use. Options: * 0 --- Nearest Neighbour (``nearest``) * 1 --- Bilinear (2x2 kernel) (``bilinear``) * 2 --- Cubic (4x4 kernel) (``cubic``) * 3 --- Cubic B-Spline (4x4 kernel) (``cubicspline``) * 4 --- Lanczos (6x6 kernel) (``lanczos``) (Type: enum) [Default: 0]
  - DATA_TYPE: Defines the format of the output raster file. Options: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **raster_data_types** :end-before: **end_raster_data_types** (Type: enum) [Default: 5]
  - ONLY_PYRAMIDS: - (Type: bool) [Default: False]
  - DIR_FOR_ROW: - (Type: bool) [Default: False]

Tool: Tile index
Algorithm ID: gdal:tileindex
Description: Builds a vector layer with a record for each input raster file, an
attribute containing the filename, and a polygon geometry outlining
the raster.
This output is suitable for use with MapServer as a raster tileindex.
This algorithm is derived from the
`GDAL Tile Index utility <https://gdal.org/programs/gdaltindex.html>`_.
**Default menu**: :menuselection:`Raster --> Miscellaneous`
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - LAYERS: The input raster files. Can be multiple files. (Type: list)
  - PATH_FIELD_NAME``
       Optional
     - [string]

       Default: 'location'
     - The output field name to hold the file path/location to the
       indexed rasters.
   * - **Store absolute path to the indexed rasters**
     - ``ABSOLUTE_PATH: Set whether the absolute path to the raster files is stored in the tile index file. By default the raster filenames will be put in the file exactly as they are specified in the command. (Type: bool) [Default: False]
  - PROJ_DIFFERENCE: Only files with same projection as files already inserted in the tile index will be inserted. Default does not check projection and accepts all inputs. (Type: bool) [Default: False]
  - OUTPUT: Specify the polygon vector layer to write the index to. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **file_output_types** :end-before: **end_file_output_types** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Save to temporary file]``]
Advanced Parameters:
  - CRS_FORMAT: Format for the CRS. One of: * 0 -- Auto (``AUTO``) * 1 -- Well-known text (``WKT``) * 2 -- EPSG (``EPSG``) * 3 -- Proj.4 (``PROJ``) (Type: enum) [Default: 0]

Tool: Viewshed
Algorithm ID: gdal:viewshed
Description: Calculates a viewshed raster from an input raster DEM using method defined in
`Wang2000 <https://gdal.org/programs/gdal_viewshed.html#wang2000>`_ for a user
defined point.
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: Input elevation raster layer (Type: str)
  - BAND: The number of the band to use as elevation (Type: str) [Default: 1]
  - OBSERVER: The location of the observer (Type: str)
  - OBSERVER_HEIGHT: The altitude of the observer, in the DEM units (Type: float) [Default: 1.0]
  - TARGET_HEIGHT: The altitude of the target element, in the DEM units (Type: float) [Default: 1.0]
  - MAX_DISTANCE: Maximum distance from observer to compute visibility, in the DEM units (Type: float) [Default: 100.0]
  - OUTPUT: Output raster layer. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **file_output_types** :end-before: **end_file_output_types** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Save to temporary file]``]
Advanced Parameters:
  - EXTRA: Add extra GDAL command line options (Type: str) [Default: None]
Toolbox: Raster projections\nDescription:
Tool: Assign projection
Algorithm ID: gdal:assignprojection
Description: Applies a coordinate system to a raster dataset.
This algorithm is derived from the
`GDAL edit utility <https://gdal.org/programs/gdal_edit.html>`_.
**Default menu**: :menuselection:`Raster --> Projections`
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT_LAYER: Input raster layer (Type: str)
  - CRS: The projection (CRS) of the output layer (Type: str)

Tool: Extract projection
Algorithm ID: gdal:extractprojection
Description: Extracts the projection of a raster file and writes it into a *world*
file with extension :file:`.wld`.
This algorithm is derived from the
`GDAL srsinfo utility <https://gdal.org/programs/gdalsrsinfo.html>`_.
**Default menu**: :menuselection:`Raster --> Projections`

Tool: Warp (reproject)
Algorithm ID: gdal:warpreproject
Description: Reprojects a raster layer into another Coordinate Reference System
(CRS).
The output file resolution and the resampling method can be chosen.
This algorithm is derived from the
`GDAL warp utility <https://gdal.org/programs/gdalwarp.html>`_.
**Default menu**: :menuselection:`Raster --> Projections`
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: Input raster layer to reproject (Type: str)
  - RESAMPLING: Pixel value resampling method to use. Options: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **raster_resampling_methods** :end-before: **end_raster_resampling_methods** (Type: enum) [Default: 0]
  - OUTPUT: Specification of the output raster layer. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **file_output_types** :end-before: **end_file_output_types** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Save to temporary file]``]
Advanced Parameters:
  - DATA_TYPE: Defines the format of the output raster file. Options: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **raster_data_types_extended** :end-before: **end_raster_data_types_extended** (Type: enum) [Default: 0]
  - MULTITHREADING: Two threads will be used to process chunks of the image and perform input/output operations simultaneously. Note that the computation itself is not multithreaded. (Type: bool) [Default: False]
Toolbox: Vector conversion\nDescription::
Tool: Convert format
Algorithm ID: gdal:convertformat
Description: Converts any OGR-supported vector layer into another OGR-supported
format.
This algorithm is derived from the
`ogr2ogr utility <https://gdal.org/programs/ogr2ogr.html>`_.
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: Input vector layer (Type: str)
  - CONVERT_ALL_LAYERS: Converts the whole dataset. Supported output formats for this option are :file:`GPKG` and :file:`GML`. (Type: bool) [Default: False]
  - OUTPUT: Specification of the output vector layer. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **file_output_types** :end-before: **end_file_output_types** For ``Save to File``, the output format has to be specified. All GDAL vector formats are supported. For ``Save to a Temporary File`` the QGIS default vector format will be used. (Type: str)

Tool: Rasterize (overwrite with attribute)
Algorithm ID: gdal:rasterize_over
Description: Overwrites a raster layer with values from a vector layer.
New values are assigned based on the attribute value of
the overlapping vector feature.
This algorithm is derived from the
`GDAL rasterize utility <https://gdal.org/programs/gdal_rasterize.html>`_.

Tool: Rasterize (overwrite with fixed value)
Algorithm ID: gdal:rasterize_over_fixed_value
Description: Overwrites parts of a raster layer with a fixed value.
The pixels to overwrite are chosen based on the supplied (overlapping)
vector layer.
This algorithm is derived from the
`GDAL rasterize utility <https://gdal.org/programs/gdal_rasterize.html>`_.

Tool: Rasterize (vector to raster)
Algorithm ID: gdal:rasterize
Description: Converts vector geometries (points, lines and polygons) into a raster
image.
This algorithm is derived from the
`GDAL rasterize utility <https://gdal.org/programs/gdal_rasterize.html>`_.
**Default menu**: :menuselection:`Raster --> Conversion`
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: Input vector layer (Type: str)
  - UNITS: Units to use when defining the output raster size/resolution. One of: * 0 --- Pixels * 1 --- Georeferenced units (Type: enum) [Default: 0]
  - WIDTH: Sets the width (if size units is "Pixels") or horizontal resolution (if size units is "Georeferenced units") of the output raster. Minimum value: 0.0. (Type: float) [Default: 0.0]
  - HEIGHT: Sets the height (if size units is "Pixels") or vertical resolution (if size units is "Georeferenced units") of the output raster. (Type: float) [Default: 0.0]
  - OUTPUT: Specification of the output raster layer. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **file_output_types** :end-before: **end_file_output_types** For ``Save to File``, the output format has to be specified. All GDAL raster formats are supported. For ``Save to a Temporary File`` the QGIS default raster format will be used. (Type: str) [Default: ``[Save to temporary file]``]
Advanced Parameters:
  - DATA_TYPE: Defines the format of the output raster file. Options: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **raster_data_types** :end-before: **end_raster_data_types** (Type: enum) [Default: 5]
  - INVERT: Burns the fixed burn value, or the burn value associated with the first feature into all parts of the image not inside the provided polygon. * - **Additional command-line parameters** Optional - ``EXTRA`` - [string] - Add extra GDAL command line options (Type: bool) [Default: False]
Toolbox: Vector geoprocessing\nDescripti:
Tool: Buffer vectors

Description: Create buffers around the features of a vector layer.
Parameters:

  - GEOMETRY: The name of the input layer geometry column to use (Type: str) [Default: 'geometry']
  - DISTANCE: Minimum: 0.0 (Type: float) [Default: 10.0]
  - DISSOLVE: If set, the result is dissolved. If no field is set for dissolving, all the buffers are dissolved into one feature. (Type: bool) [Default: False]

Tool: Clip vector by extent

Description: Clips any OGR-supported vector file to a given extent.
This algorithm is derived from the

  - OUTPUT: Specify the output (clipped) layer. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **file_output_types** :end-before: **end_file_output_types** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Save to temporary file]``]

Description: Clips any OGR-supported vector layer by a mask polygon layer.

Tool: Dissolve
Algorithm ID: gdal:dissolve
Description: Dissolve (combine) geometries that have the same value for
a given attribute / field.
The output geometries are multipart.
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: The input layer to dissolve (Type: str)
  - GEOMETRY: The name of the input layer geometry column to use for dissolving. (Type: str) [Default: 'geometry']
  - OUTPUT: Specify the output layer. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **file_output_types** :end-before: **end_file_output_types** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Save to temporary file]``]
Advanced Parameters:
  - EXPLODE_COLLECTIONS: Produce one feature for each geometry in any kind of geometry collection in the source file (Type: bool) [Default: False]
  - KEEP_ATTRIBUTES: Keep all attributes from the input layer (Type: bool) [Default: False]
  - COUNT_FEATURES: Count the dissolved features and include it in the output layer. (Type: bool) [Default: False]
  - COMPUTE_AREA: Compute the area and perimeter of dissolved features and include them in the output layer (Type: bool) [Default: False]
  - COMPUTE_STATISTICS: Calculate statistics (min, max, sum and mean) for the numeric attribute specified and include them in the output layer (Type: bool) [Default: False]

Tool: Offset curve
Algorithm ID: gdal:offsetcurve
Description: Offsets lines by a specified distance.
Positive distances will offset lines to the left, and negative
distances will offset them to the right.

  - GEOMETRY: The name of the input layer geometry column to use (Type: str) [Default: 'geometry']
  - DISTANCE: - (Type: float) [Default: 10.0]
  - OUTPUT: Specify the output line layer. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **file_output_types** :end-before: **end_file_output_types** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Save to temporary file]``]

Tool: One side buffer
Algorithm ID: gdal:onesidebuffer
Description: Creates a buffer on one side (right or left) of the lines in a line
vector layer.
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: The input line layer (Type: str)
  - GEOMETRY: The name of the input layer geometry column to use (Type: str) [Default: 'geometry']
  - DISTANCE: - (Type: float) [Default: 10.0]
  - BUFFER_SIDE: One of: * 0 --- Right * 1 --- Left (Type: enum) [Default: 0]
  - DISSOLVE: If set, the result is dissolved. If no field is set for dissolving, all the buffers are dissolved into one feature. (Type: bool) [Default: False]
  - EXPLODE_COLLECTIONS: - (Type: bool) [Default: False]
  - OUTPUT: Specify the output buffer layer. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **file_output_types** :end-before: **end_file_output_types** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Save to temporary file]``]

Tool: Points along lines
Algorithm ID: gdal:pointsalonglines
Description: Generates a point on each line of a line vector layer at a distance
from start.
The distance is provided as a fraction of the line length.

Basic Parameters:

  - DISTANCE: - (Type: float) [Default: 0.5 (middle of the line)]
  - OUTPUT: Specify the output point layer. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **file_output_types** :end-before: **end_file_output_types** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Save to temporary file]``]
Toolbox: Vector miscellaneous\nDescripti:
Tool: Build virtual vector
Algorithm ID: gdal:buildvirtualvector
Description: Creates a virtual vector layer that contains a set of vector layers.
The output virtual vector layer will not be opened in the current
project.
This algorithm is especially useful in case another algorithm needs
multiple layers but accept only one ``vrt`` in which the layers are
specified.
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: Select the vector layers you want to use to build the virtual vector (Type: list)
  - UNIONED: Check if you want to unite all the vectors in a single ``vrt`` file (Type: bool) [Default: False]
  - OUTPUT: Specify the output layer containing only the duplicates. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **file_output_types** :end-before: **end_file_output_types** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Save to temporary file]``]

Tool: Execute SQL
Algorithm ID: gdal:executesql
Description: Runs a simple or complex query with SQL syntax on the source layer.
The result of the query will be added as a new layer.
This algorithm is derived from the
`GDAL ogr2ogr utility <https://gdal.org/programs/ogr2ogr.html>`_.
Parameters:

  - OUTPUT: Specification of the output layer. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **file_output_types** :end-before: **end_file_output_types** For ``Save to File``, the output format has to be specified. All GDAL vector formats are supported. For ``Save to a Temporary File`` the default output vector layer format will be used. (Type: str)

Tool: Export to PostgreSQL (available connections)
Algorithm ID: gdal:importvectorintopostgisdatabaseavailableconnections
Description: Imports vector layers inside a PostgreSQL database on the basis of
an available connection.
The connection has to
:ref:`be defined properly <vector_create_stored_connection>`
beforehand.
Be aware that the checkboxes 'Save Username' and 'Save Password' are
activated.
Then you can use the algorithm.
This algorithm is derived from the
`GDAL ogr2ogr utility <https://gdal.org/programs/ogr2ogr.html>`_.
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - DATABASE: The PostgreSQL database to connect to (Type: str)
  - INPUT: OGR-supported vector layer to export to the database (Type: str)
  - GTYPE: Defines the output geometry type. One of: * 0 --- * 1 --- NONE * 2 --- GEOMETRY * 3 --- POINT * 4 --- LINESTRING * 5 --- POLYGON * 6 --- GEOMETRYCOLLECTION * 7 --- MULTIPOINT * 8 --- MULTIPOLYGON * 9 --- MULTILINESTRING (Type: enum) [Default: 0]

Tool: Export to PostgreSQL (new connection)
Algorithm ID: gdal:importvectorintopostgisdatabasenewconnection
Description: Imports vector layers inside a PostgreSQL database. A new connection
to the PostGIS database must be created.
This algorithm is derived from the
`GDAL ogr2ogr utility <https://gdal.org/programs/ogr2ogr.html>`_.
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: OGR-supported vector layer to export to the database (Type: str)
  - GTYPE: Defines the output geometry type. One of: * 0 --- * 1 --- NONE * 2 --- GEOMETRY * 3 --- POINT * 4 --- LINESTRING * 5 --- POLYGON * 6 --- GEOMETRYCOLLECTION * 7 --- MULTIPOINT * 8 --- MULTIPOLYGON * 9 --- MULTILINESTRING (Type: enum) [Default: 0]

Tool: Vector Information

  - OUTPUT: Specify the output HTML file that includes the file information. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **file_output_types** :end-before: **end_file_output_types** If no HTML-file is defined the output will be written to a temporary file (Type: str) [Default: ``[Save to temporary file]``]

Toolbox: Cartography\nDescription: This:
Tool: Align points to features
Algorithm ID: native:angletonearest
Description: Calculates the rotation required to align point features with their nearest
feature from another reference layer. A new field is added to the output layer
which is filled with the angle (in degrees, clockwise) to the nearest reference
feature.
Optionally, the output layer's symbology can be set to automatically use the
calculated rotation field to rotate marker symbols.
If desired, a maximum distance to use when aligning points can be set,
to avoid aligning isolated points to distant features.
.. hint:: This algorithm is designed for use cases like aligning building
 point symbols to follow the nearest road direction.
of point features
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: Point features to calculate the rotation for (Type: str)
  - REFERENCE_LAYER: Layer to find the closest feature from for rotation calculation (Type: str)
  - FIELD_NAME: Field in which to store the rotation value. (Type: str) [Default: 'rotation']
  - APPLY_SYMBOLOGY: Rotates the symbol marker of the features using the angle field value (Type: bool) [Default: True]
  - OUTPUT: Specify the rotated output vector layer. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **layer_output_types** :end-before: **end_layer_output_types** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Save to temporary file]``]

Tool: Combine style databases
Algorithm ID: native:combinestyles
Description: Combines multiple QGIS style databases into a single style database.
If items of the same type with the same name exist in different source
databases these will be renamed to have unique names in the output combined database.
.. seealso:: :ref:`qgisstylefromproject`
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: Files containing QGIS style items (Type: list)
  - OBJECTS: Types of style items in the input databases you would like to put in the new database. These can be: * 0 --- :ref:`Symbols <edit_symbol>` * 1 --- :ref:`Color ramps <color-ramp>` * 2 --- :ref:`Text formats <text_format>` * 3 --- :ref:`Label settings <showlabels>` (Type: enum)
  - OUTPUT: Output :file:`.XML` file combining the selected style items. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **file_output_types** :end-before: **end_file_output_types** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Save to temporary file]``]

Tool: Create categorized renderer from styles
Algorithm ID: native:categorizeusingstyle
Description: Sets a vector layer's renderer to a categorized renderer using matching symbols
from a style database. If no style file is specified, symbols from the user's
current :ref:`symbol library <vector_symbol_library>` are used instead.
A specified expression or field is used to create categories for the renderer.
Each category is individually matched to the symbols which exist within
the specified QGIS XML style database. Whenever a matching symbol name is found,
the category's symbol will be set to this matched symbol.
If desired, outputs can also be tables containing lists of the categories which
could not be matched to symbols, and symbols which were not matched to categories.
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: Vector layer to apply a categorized style to (Type: str)
  - FIELD: Field or expression to categorize the features (Type: str)
  - STYLE: File (:file:`.XML`) containing the symbols to apply to the input layer categories. The file can be obtained from the Style Manager :ref:`Share symbols <share_symbols>` tool. If no file is specified, QGIS local symbols library is used. (Type: str)
  - CASE_SENSITIVE: If True (checked), applies a case sensitive comparison between the categories and symbols names (Type: bool) [Default: False]
  - TOLERANT: If True (checked), non-alphanumeric characters in the categories and symbols names will be ignored, allowing greater tolerance during the match. (Type: bool) [Default: False]

Tool: Create style database from project
Algorithm ID: native:stylefromproject
Description: Extracts all style objects (symbols, color ramps, text formats and
label settings) from a QGIS project.
The extracted symbols are saved to a QGIS style database (:file:`XML` format),
which can be managed and imported via the :ref:`Style Manager <vector_style_manager>`
dialog.
.. seealso:: :ref:`qgiscombinestyles`
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - OBJECTS: Types of style items in the input project you would like to put in the new database. These can be: * 0 --- :ref:`Symbols <edit_symbol>` * 1 --- :ref:`Color ramps <color-ramp>` * 2 --- :ref:`Text formats <text_format>` * 3 --- :ref:`Label settings <showlabels>` (Type: enum)
  - OUTPUT: Specify the output :file:`.XML` file for the selected style items. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **file_output_types** :end-before: **end_file_output_types** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Save to temporary file]``]

Tool: Export atlas layout as image
Algorithm ID: native:atlaslayouttoimage
Description: Exports the atlas of a print layout as image files (e.g. PNG or JPEG images).
If a coverage layer is set, the selected layout's atlas settings exposed
in this algorithm will be overwritten. In this case, an empty filter or
sort by expression will turn those settings off.
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - LAYOUT: Layout to export (Type: str)
  - FILTER_EXPRESSION: Expression to use to filter out atlas features (Type: str)
  - FILENAME_EXPRESSION: Expression for use to generate filenames (Type: str) [Default: 'output\_'||\@atlas_featurenumber]
  - FOLDER: Destination folder where the images will be generated (Type: str)
Advanced Parameters:
  - EXTENSION: File format of the generated output(s). The list of available formats varies depending on OS and installed drivers. (Type: enum) [Default: png]
  - GEOREFERENCE: Determines if a world file should be generated (Type: bool) [Default: True]
  - INCLUDE_METADATA: Determines if RDF metadata (title, author, ...) should be generated (Type: bool) [Default: True]
  - ANTIALIAS: Determines if antialiasing should be enabled (Type: bool) [Default: True]

Tool: Export atlas layout as PDF (multiple files)
Algorithm ID: native:atlaslayouttomultiplepdf
Description: Exports the atlas of a print layout to multiple PDF files.
If a coverage layer is set, the selected layout's atlas settings exposed
in this algorithm will be overwritten. In this case, an empty filter or
sort by expression will turn those settings off.
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - LAYOUT: Layout to export (Type: str)
  - FILTER_EXPRESSION: Expression to use to filter out atlas features (Type: str)
  - OUTPUT_FOLDER: Destination folder for the output PDF files. (Type: str)
Advanced Parameters:
  - FORCE_VECTOR: Determines if vectorial data should be left as vectors (Type: bool) [Default: False]
  - FORCE_RASTER: Forces all the items in the map to be rasterized. This parameter takes precedence over the ``FORCE_VECTOR`` parameter. (Type: bool) [Default: False]
  - GEOREFERENCE: Determines if a world file should be generated (Type: bool) [Default: True]
  - INCLUDE_METADATA: Determines if RDF metadata (title, author, ...) should be generated (Type: bool) [Default: True]
  - DISABLE_TILED: Determines if raster should be tiled (Type: bool) [Default: False]
  - SIMPLIFY: Determines if geometries should be simplified to reduce output file size (Type: bool) [Default: True]
  - TEXT_FORMAT: Determines if text should be exported as path or text objects. Possible options are: * 0 - Always export text as paths (recommended) * 1 - Always export texts as text objects (Type: enum) [Default: 0]
  - IMAGE_COMPRESSION: Determines compression level of the image and how suitable the file could be for printing outputs or post-production in external applications. Possible options are: * 0 - Lossy (JPEG) * 1 - Lossless (Type: enum) [Default: 0]

Tool: Export atlas layout as PDF (single file)
Algorithm ID: native:atlaslayouttopdf
Description: Exports the atlas of a print layout as a single PDF file.
If a coverage layer is set, the selected layout's atlas settings exposed
in this algorithm will be overwritten. In this case, an empty filter or

Advanced Parameters:
  - FORCE_VECTOR: Determines if vectorial data should be left as vectors (Type: bool) [Default: False]
  - FORCE_RASTER: Forces all the items in the map to be rasterized. This parameter takes precedence over the ``FORCE_VECTOR`` parameter. (Type: bool) [Default: False]
  - GEOREFERENCE: Determines if a world file should be generated (Type: bool) [Default: True]
  - INCLUDE_METADATA: Determines if RDF metadata (title, author, ...) should be generated (Type: bool) [Default: True]
  - DISABLE_TILED: Determines if raster should be tiled (Type: bool) [Default: False]
  - SIMPLIFY: Determines if geometries should be simplified to reduce output file size (Type: bool) [Default: True]
  - TEXT_FORMAT: Determines if text should be exported as path or text objects. Possible options are: * 0 - Always export text as paths (recommended) * 1 - Always export texts as text objects (Type: enum) [Default: 0]
  - IMAGE_COMPRESSION: Determines compression level of the image and how suitable the file could be for printing outputs or post-production in external applications. Possible options are: * 0 - Lossy (JPEG) * 1 - Lossless (Type: enum) [Default: 0]

Tool: Extract labels
Algorithm ID: native:extractlabels
Description: Extracts label information from a rendered map at a given extent and scale.
If a map theme is provided, the rendered map will match the visibility and
symbology of that theme. If left blank, all visible layers from the project
will be used.
Extracted label information include: position (served as point geometries),
the associated layer name and feature ID, label text, rotation (in degree,
clockwise), multiline alignment, and font details.
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - EXTENT: Extent of the map to extract the labels from .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **extent_options** :end-before: **end_extent_options** (Type: str)
  - SCALE: Extracted labels will be rendered using their properties set at this scale. (Type: str)
  - OUTPUT: Specify the output vector layer for the extent(s). One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **layer_output_types** :end-before: **end_layer_output_types** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Create temporary layer]``]

Tool: Print layout map extent to layer
Algorithm ID: native:printlayoutmapextenttolayer
Description: Creates a polygon layer containing the extent of a print layout map item
(or items), with attributes specifying the map size (in layout units,
i.e. the :ref:`reference map <reference_map>` units), scale and rotation.
If the map item parameter is specified, then only the matching map extent will
be exported. If it is not specified, all map extents from the layout will be exported.
Optionally, a specific output CRS can be specified. If it is not specified,
the original map item CRS will be used.
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - LAYOUT: A print layout in the current project (Type: enum)
  - OUTPUT: Specify the output vector layer for the extent(s). One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **layer_output_types** :end-before: **end_layer_output_types** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Create temporary layer]``]

:file:`QML` file.
No new output are created: the style is immediately assigned to the layer.
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: Input layer you want to apply the style to (Type: str)
  - STYLE: Path to the ``.qml`` file of the style (Type: str)

Tool: Topological coloring
Algorithm ID: qgis:topologicalcoloring
Description: Assigns a color index to polygon features in such a way that no adjacent polygons
share the same color index, whilst minimizing the number of colors required.
The algorithm allows choice of method to use when assigning colors.
A minimum number of colors can be specified if desired. The color index is saved
to a new attribute named **color_id**.
The following example shows the algorithm with four different colors chosen; as you
can see each color class has the same amount of features.
  Topological colors example
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: The input polygon layer (Type: str)
  - MIN_COLORS: The minimum number of colors to assign. Minimum 1, maximum 1000. (Type: int) [Default: 4]
  - MIN_DISTANCE: Prevent nearby (but non-touching) features from being assigned equal colors. Minimum 0.0. (Type: float) [Default: 0.0]

This mode can be useful to help avoid large features resulting in one of the colors appearing more dominant on a colored map. * 2 --- By distance between colors Assigns colors in order to maximize the distance between features of the same color. This mode helps to create a more uniform distribution of colors across a map. (Type: enum) [Default: 0]
  - OUTPUT: Specify the output layer. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **layer_output_types** :end-before: **end_layer_output_types** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Create temporary layer]``]
