Toolbox: Interpolation\nDescription: Thi:
Tool: Heatmap (kernel density estimation)
Algorithm ID: qgis:heatmapkerneldensityestimation
Description: Creates a density (heatmap) raster of an input point vector layer
using kernel density estimation.
The density is calculated based on the number of points in a location,
with larger numbers of clustered points resulting in larger values.
Heatmaps allow easy identification of *hotspots* and clustering of
points.
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: Point vector layer to use for the heatmap (Type: str)
  - RADIUS: Heatmap search radius (or kernel bandwidth) in map units. The radius specifies the distance around a point at which the influence of the point will be felt. Larger values result in greater smoothing, but smaller values may show finer details and variation in point density. (Type: float) [Default: 100.0]
  - PIXEL_SIZE: Pixel size of the output raster layer in layer units. In the GUI, the size can be specified by the number of rows (``Number of rows``) / columns (``Number of columns``) **or** the pixel size( ``Pixel Size X`` / ``Pixel Size Y``). Increasing the number of rows or columns will decrease the cell size and increase the file size of the output raster. The values in ``Rows``, ``Columns``, ``Pixel Size X`` and ``Pixel Size Y`` will be updated simultaneously - doubling the number of rows will double the number of columns, and the cell size will be halved. The extent of the output raster will remain the same (approximately). (Type: float) [Default: 0.1]
  - KERNEL: Controls the rate at which the influence of a point decreases as the distance from the point increases. Different kernels decay at different rates, so a triweight kernel gives features greater weight for distances closer to the point then the Epanechnikov kernel does. Consequently, triweight results in “sharper” hotspots and Epanechnikov results in “smoother” hotspots. There are many shapes available (please see the `Wikipedia page <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kernel_(statistics)#Kernel_functions_in_common_use>`_ for further information): * 0 --- Quartic * 1 --- Triangular * 2 --- Uniform * 3 --- Triweight * 4 --- Epanechnikov (Type: enum) [Default: *0*]
  - OUTPUT_VALUE: Allow to change the values of the output heatmap raster. One of: * 0 --- Raw * 1 --- Scaled (Type: enum) [Default: *Raw*]
  - OUTPUT: Specify the output raster layer with kernel density values. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **file_output_types** :end-before: **end_file_output_types** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Save to temporary file]``]

Tool: IDW Interpolation
Algorithm ID: qgis:idwinterpolation
Description: Generates an Inverse Distance Weighted (IDW) interpolation of a point
vector layer.
Sample points are weighted during interpolation such that the
influence of one point relative to another declines with distance from
the unknown point you want to create.
The IDW interpolation method also has some disadvantages: the quality
of the interpolation result can decrease, if the distribution of
sample data points is uneven.
Furthermore, maximum and minimum values in the interpolated surface
can only occur at sample data points.
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INTERPOLATION_DATA: Vector layer(s) and field(s) to use for the interpolation, coded in a string (see the ``ParameterInterpolationData`` class in :source:`InterpolationWidgets <python/plugins/processing/algs/qgis/ui/InterpolationWidgets.py>` for more details). The following GUI elements are provided to compose the interpolation data string: * **Vector layer** [vector: any] * **Interpolation attribute** [tablefield: numeric]: Attribute to use in the interpolation * **Use Z-coordinate for interpolation** [boolean]: Uses the layer's stored Z values ( For each of the added layer-field combinations, a type can be chosen: * :guilabel:`Points` * :guilabel:`Structured lines` * :guilabel:`Break lines` In the string, the layer-field elements are separated by ``'::|::'``. The sub-elements of the layer-field elements are separated by ``'::~::'``. (Type: str) [Default: False)]
  - DISTANCE_COEFFICIENT: Sets the distance coefficient for the interpolation. Minimum: 0.0, maximum: 100.0. (Type: float) [Default: 2.0]
  - EXTENT: Extent of the output raster layer. .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **extent_options** :end-before: **end_extent_options** (Type: str)
  - PIXEL_SIZE: Pixel size of the output raster layer in layer units. In the GUI, the size can be specified by the number of rows (``Number of rows``) / columns (``Number of columns``) **or** the pixel size( ``Pixel Size X`` / ``Pixel Size Y``). Increasing the number of rows or columns will decrease the cell size and increase the file size of the output raster. The values in ``Rows``, ``Columns``, ``Pixel Size X`` and ``Pixel Size Y`` will be updated simultaneously - doubling the number of rows will double the number of columns, and the cell size will be halved. The extent of the output raster will remain the same (approximately). (Type: float) [Default: 0.1]
  - OUTPUT: Raster layer of interpolated values. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **file_output_types** :end-before: **end_file_output_types** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Save to temporary file]``]

Tool: Line Density
Algorithm ID: native:linedensity
Description: Calculates for each raster cell, the density measure of linear
features within a circular neighbourhood. This measure is obtained by
summing all the line segments intersecting the circular neighbourhood
and dividing this sum by the area of such neighbourhood. 
A weighting factor can be applied to the line segments. 
  Line density example. Input layer source: Roads Overijssel - The
  Netherlands (OSM).
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: Input vector layer containing line features (Type: str)
  - WEIGHT: Field of the layer containing the weight factor to use during the calculation (Type: float)
  - RADIUS: Radius of the circular neighbourhood. Units can be specified here. (Type: int) [Default: 10]
  - PIXEL_SIZE: Pixel size of the output raster layer in layer units. The raster has square pixels. (Type: int) [Default: 10]
  - OUTPUT: The output as a raster layer. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **file_output_types** :end-before: **end_file_output_types** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Save to temporary file]``]

Tool: TIN Interpolation
Algorithm ID: qgis:tininterpolation
Description: Generates a Triangulated Irregular Network (TIN) interpolation of a
point vector layer.
With the TIN method you can create a surface formed by triangles of
nearest neighbor points.
To do this, circumcircles around selected sample points are created
and their intersections are connected to a network of non overlapping
and as compact as possible triangles.
The resulting surfaces are not smooth.
The algorithm creates both the raster layer of the interpolated values
and the vector line layer with the triangulation boundaries.
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INTERPOLATION_DATA: Vector layer(s) and field(s) to use for the interpolation, coded in a string (see the ``ParameterInterpolationData`` class in :source:`InterpolationWidgets <python/plugins/processing/algs/qgis/ui/InterpolationWidgets.py>` for more details). The following GUI elements are provided to compose the interpolation data string: * **Vector layer** [vector: any] * **Interpolation attribute** [tablefield: numeric]: Attribute to use in the interpolation * **Use Z-coordinate for interpolation** [boolean]: Uses the layer's stored Z values ( For each of the added layer-field combinations, a type can be chosen: * :guilabel:`Points` * :guilabel:`Structured lines` * :guilabel:`Break lines` In the string, the layer-field elements are separated by ``'::|::'``. The sub-elements of the layer-field elements are separated by ``'::~::'``. (Type: str) [Default: False)]
  - METHOD: Set the interpolation method to be used. One of: * :guilabel:`Linear` * :guilabel:`Clough-Toucher (cubic)` (Type: enum) [Default: 0]
  - EXTENT: Extent of the output raster layer. .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **extent_options** :end-before: **end_extent_options** (Type: str)
  - PIXEL_SIZE: Pixel size of the output raster layer in layer units. In the GUI, the size can be specified by the number of rows (``Number of rows``) / columns (``Number of columns``) **or** the pixel size( ``Pixel Size X`` / ``Pixel Size Y``). Increasing the number of rows or columns will decrease the cell size and increase the file size of the output raster. The values in ``Rows``, ``Columns``, ``Pixel Size X`` and ``Pixel Size Y`` will be updated simultaneously - doubling the number of rows will double the number of columns, and the cell size will be halved. The extent of the output raster will remain the same (approximately). (Type: float) [Default: 0.1]
  - OUTPUT: The output TIN interpolation as a raster layer. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **file_output_types** :end-before: **end_file_output_types** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Save to temporary file]``]
  - TRIANGULATION: The output TIN as a vector layer. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **layer_output_types_skip** :end-before: **end_layer_output_types_skip** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Skip output]``]

  - VECTOR_OPTION: Coordinate type of vector value exportation. * 0 --- Cartesian (x,y) * 1 --- Polar (magnitude, degree) * 2 --- Cartesian and polar (Type: enum)
  - OUTPUT: Specification of the output file. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **layer_output_types** :end-before: **end_layer_output_types** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Create temporary layer]``]

Tool: Export mesh vertices
Algorithm ID: native:exportmeshvertices
Description: Exports a mesh layer's vertices to a point vector layer,
with the dataset values on vertices as attribute values.
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: The mesh layer to export data from (Type: str)
  - DATASET_GROUPS: The dataset groups (Type: list)
  - DATASET_TIME: The time range to take into account * 0 --- Current canvas time * 1 --- Defined date/time * 2 --- Dataset group time step (Type: str)

Tool: Export time series values from points of a mesh dataset
Algorithm ID: native:meshexporttimeseries
Description: Extracts a mesh dataset's time series values from points contained in a vector layer.
If the time step is kept to its default value (0 hours), the time step used
is the one of the two first datasets of the first selected dataset group.
Parameters:

  - DATASET_GROUPS: The dataset groups (Type: list)

Tool: Rasterize mesh dataset
Algorithm ID: native:meshrasterize
Description: Creates a raster layer from a mesh dataset.
For data on volume (3D stacked dataset values), the exported dataset
values are averaged on faces using the method defined in :ref:`the mesh layer
properties <mesh_stacked_averaging>` (default is Multi level averaging method).
1D meshes are not supported.

  - OUTPUT: Specification of the output file. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **file_output_types** :end-before: **end_file_output_types** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Save to temporary file]``]

Tool: TIN mesh creation
Algorithm ID: native:tinmeshcreation
Description: Creates a TIN mesh layer from vector layers.
The TIN mesh is created using a Delaunay triangulation.

  - OUTPUT_MESH: Specification of the output file. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **file_output_types** :end-before: **end_file_output_types** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Save to temporary file]``]
Toolbox: Modeler tools\nDescription: Thi:
Tool: Calculate expression
Algorithm ID: native:calculateexpression
Description: It calculates the result of a QGIS expression and eliminates 
the need to use the same expression multiple times throughout 
a model when the same result is required more than once. 
Additionally, it enables use cases that would otherwise not be
possible. For instance, you can generate a timestamp value once
and use it multiple times within the model, if the timestamp 
were recalculated every time, the values would vary during the
model's runtime.
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: Expression to calculate (Type: str)

Tool: Conditional branch
Algorithm ID: native:condition
Description: Adds a conditional branch into a model,
allowing parts of the model to be executed based on
the result of an expression evaluation. Mostly by using
tool dependencies to control the flow of a model.
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - BRANCH: Name of the condition (Type: str)
  - CONDITION: Expression to evaluate (Type: str)

Tool: Create directory
Algorithm ID: native:createdirectory
Description: Creates a new directory on a file system.
Directories will be created recursively, creating all required parent
directories in order to construct the full specified directory path.
No errors will be raised if the directory already exists.
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - PATH: Folder path to create (Type: str)

Tool: Feature filter
Algorithm ID: native:filter
Description: Filters features from the input layer and redirects
them to one or several outputs.
If you do not know about any attribute names that are common to all
possible input layers, filtering is only possible on the feature
geometry and general record mechanisms, such as ``$id`` and ``uuid``.
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: The input layer. (Type: str)

Tool: Filter layers by type
Algorithm ID: native:filterlayersbytype
Description: Filters layers by their type. Incoming layers will be directed
to different outputs based on whether they are a vector or raster layer.
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: Generic Map Layer (Type: str)

Tool: Load layer into project
Algorithm ID: native:loadlayer
Description: Loads a layer to the current project.
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: Layer to load in the legend (Type: str)
  - NAME: Name of the loaded layer (Type: str)

Tool: Raise exception
Algorithm ID: native:raiseexception
Description: Raises an exception and cancels a model's execution.
The exception message can be customized, and optionally an expression based condition
can be specified. If an expression condition is used, then the exception will only
be raised if the expression result is true. A false result indicates that no exception
will be raised, and the model execution can continue uninterrupted.
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - MESSAGE: Message to display (Type: str)

Tool: Raise message
Algorithm ID: native:raisemessage
Description: Raises an information message in the log.
The message can be customized, and optionally an expression based condition
can be specified. If an expression condition is used, then the message will only
be logged if the expression result is true. A false result indicates that no message
will be logged.
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - MESSAGE: Message to display (Type: str)

Tool: Raise warning
Algorithm ID: native:raisewarning
Description: Raises a warning message in the log.
The warning message can be customized, and optionally an expression based condition
can be specified. If an expression condition is used, then the warning will only
be logged if the expression result is true. A false result indicates that no warning
will be logged.
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - MESSAGE: Message to display (Type: str)

Tool: Rename layer
Algorithm ID: native:renamelayer
Description: Renames a layer.
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: Layer to rename (Type: str)
  - NAME: The new name of the layer (Type: str)

Tool: Save log to file
Algorithm ID: native:savelog
Description: Saves the model's execution log to a file.
Optionally, the log can be saved in a HTML formatted version.
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - USE_HTML: Use HTML formatting (Type: str) [Default: False]

Tool: Set project variable
Algorithm ID: native:setprojectvariable
Description: Sets an expression variable for the current project.
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - NAME: Name of the variable (Type: str)
  - VALUE: Value to be stored (Type: str)

Tool: String concatenation
Algorithm ID: native:stringconcatenation
Description: Concatenates two strings into a single one in the Processing Modeler.
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT_1: First string (Type: str)
  - INPUT_2: Second string (Type: str)

Tool: Variable distance buffer
Algorithm ID: qgis:variabledistancebuffer
Description: .. warning:: This algorithm is deprecated and can be removed
  anytime. Prefer using :ref:`qgisbuffer` algorithm instead.
Computes a buffer area for all the features in an input layer.
The size of the buffer for a given feature is defined by an
attribute, so it allows different features to have different buffer
sizes.
.. seealso:: :ref:`qgisbuffer`
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: Input vector layer (Type: str)
  - DISTANCE: Attribute for the distance radius of the buffer (Type: str)
  - SEGMENTS: Controls the number of line segments to use to approximate a quarter circle when creating rounded offsets. (Type: float) [Default: *5*]
  - DISSOLVE: Choose to dissolve the final buffer, resulting in a single feature covering all input features. Normal and dissolved buffer (Type: bool) [Default: *False*]
  - END_CAP_STYLE: Controls how line endings are handled in the buffer. Round, flat and square cap styles (Type: enum) [Default: Round]
  - JOIN_STYLE: Specifies whether round, miter or beveled joins should be used when offsetting corners in a line. (Type: enum) [Default: Round]
  - MITER_LIMIT: Only applicable for mitered join styles, and controls the maximum distance from the offset curve to use when creating a mitered join. (Type: float) [Default: 2.0]
Toolbox: Network analysis\nDescription::
Tool: Service area (from layer)
Algorithm ID: qgis:serviceareafromlayer
Description: Returns all the edges or parts of edges of a network that can be
reached within a distance or a time, starting from a point layer.
This allows evaluation of accessibility within a network, e.g. what
are the places I can navigate to on a road network without spending
cost greater than a given value (the cost can be distance or time).
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: Line vector layer representing the network to be covered (Type: str)
  - START_POINTS: Point vector layer whose features are used as start points to generate the service areas (Type: str)
  - STRATEGY: The type of path to calculate. One of: * 0 --- Shortest * 1 --- Fastest (Type: enum) [Default: 0]
  - TRAVEL_COST: The value is estimated as a distance (in the network layer units) when looking for the *Shortest* path and as time (in hours) for the *Fastest* path. (Type: int) [Default: 0]
  - OUTPUT_LINES: Specify the output line layer for the service area. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **layer_output_types_skip** :end-before: **end_layer_output_types_skip** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Create temporary layer]``]
  - OUTPUT: Specify the output point layer for the service area boundary nodes. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **layer_output_types_skip** :end-before: **end_layer_output_types_skip** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Skip output]``]
Advanced Parameters:
  - DEFAULT_DIRECTION: If a feature has no value set in the direction field or if no direction field is set, then this direction value is used. One of: * 0 --- Forward direction * 1 --- Backward direction * 2 --- Both directions (Type: enum) [Default: 2]
  - DEFAULT_SPEED: Value to use to calculate the travel time if no speed field is provided for an edge (Type: float) [Default: 50.0]
  - TOLERANCE: Two lines with nodes closer than the specified tolerance are considered connected .. **end_network_advanced_parameters** .. list-table:: :widths: 20 20 20 40 (Type: float) [Default: 0.0]
  - INCLUDE_BOUNDS: Creates a point layer output with two points for each edge at the boundaries of the service area. One point is the start of that edge, the other is the end. (Type: bool) [Default: False]

Tool: Service area (from point)
Algorithm ID: native:serviceareafrompoint
Description: Returns all the edges or parts of edges of a network that can be
reached within a given distance or time, starting from a point
feature.
This allows the evaluation of accessibility within a network, e.g.
what are the places I can navigate to on a road network without
spending a cost greater than a given value (the cost can be distance
or time).
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: Line vector layer representing the network to be covered (Type: str)
  - START_POINT: Coordinate of the point to calculate the service area around. (Type: str)
  - STRATEGY: The type of path to calculate. One of: * 0 --- Shortest * 1 --- Fastest (Type: enum) [Default: 0]
  - TRAVEL_COST: The value is estimated as a distance (in the network layer units) when looking for the *Shortest* path and as time (in hours) for the *Fastest* path. (Type: int) [Default: 0]
  - OUTPUT_LINES: Specify the output line layer for the service area. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **layer_output_types_skip** :end-before: **end_layer_output_types_skip** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Create temporary layer]``]
  - OUTPUT: Specify the output point layer for the service area boundary nodes. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **layer_output_types_skip** :end-before: **end_layer_output_types_skip** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Skip output]``]
Advanced Parameters:
  - INCLUDE_BOUNDS: Creates a point layer output with two points for each edge at the boundaries of the service area. One point is the start of that edge, the other is the end. (Type: bool) [Default: False]

Tool: Shortest path (layer to point)
Algorithm ID: native:shortestpathlayertopoint
Description: Computes the optimal (shortest or fastest) routes from multiple start
points defined by a vector layer and a given end point.
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: Line vector layer representing the network to be covered (Type: str)
  - STRATEGY: The type of path to calculate. One of: * 0 --- Shortest * 1 --- Fastest (Type: enum) [Default: 0]
  - START_POINTS: Point vector layer whose features are used as start points of the routes (Type: str)
  - END_POINT: Point feature representing the end point of the routes (Type: str)
  - OUTPUT: Specify the output line layer for the shortest paths. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **layer_output_types** :end-before: **end_layer_output_types** (Type: str)
Advanced Parameters:
  - OUTPUT: Line layer of the shortest or fastest path from each of the start points to the end point (Type: str)

Tool: Shortest path (point to layer)
Algorithm ID: native:shortestpathpointtolayer
Description: Computes the optimal (shortest or fastest) routes between a given
start point and multiple end points defined by a point vector layer.
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: Line vector layer representing the network to be covered (Type: str)
  - STRATEGY: The type of path to calculate. One of: * 0 --- Shortest * 1 --- Fastest (Type: enum) [Default: 0]
  - START_POINT: Point feature representing the start point of the routes (Type: str)
  - END_POINTS: Point vector layer whose features are used as end points of the routes (Type: str)
  - OUTPUT: Specify the output line layer for the shortest paths. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **layer_output_types** :end-before: **end_layer_output_types** (Type: str)
Advanced Parameters:
  - OUTPUT: Line layer of the shortest or fastest path from each of the start points to the end point (Type: str)

Tool: Shortest path (point to point)
Algorithm ID: native:shortestpathpointtopoint
Description: Computes the optimal (shortest or fastest) route between a given start
point and a given end point.
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: Line vector layer representing the network to be covered (Type: str)
  - STRATEGY: The type of path to calculate. One of: * 0 --- Shortest * 1 --- Fastest (Type: enum) [Default: 0]
  - START_POINT: Point feature representing the start point of the routes (Type: str)
  - END_POINT: Point feature representing the end point of the routes (Type: str)
  - OUTPUT: Specify the output line layer for the shortest paths. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **layer_output_types** :end-before: **end_layer_output_types** (Type: str)
Advanced Parameters:
  - OUTPUT: Line layer of the shortest or fastest path from each of the start point to the end point (Type: str)
Toolbox: Plots\nDescription: This toolbo:
Tool: Bar plot
Algorithm ID: qgis:barplot
Description: Creates a bar plot from a category and a layer field.

Basic Parameters:

  - NAME_FIELD: Categorical field to use for grouping the bars (X axis) (Type: str)

Tool: Box plot
Algorithm ID: qgis:boxplot
Description: Creates a box plot from a category field and a numerical layer field.

Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: Input vector layer (Type: str)
  - NAME_FIELD: Categorical field to use for grouping the boxes (X axis) (Type: str)
  - VALUE_FIELD: Value to use for the plot (Y axis). (Type: str)

  - OUTPUT: Specify the HTML file for the plot. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **file_output_types** :end-before: **end_file_output_types** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Save to temporary file]``]

  - OUTPUT: Specify the HTML file for the plot. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **file_output_types** :end-before: **end_file_output_types** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Save to temporary file]``]

Tool: Polar plot
Algorithm ID: qgis:polarplot

Two fields must be entered as parameters: one that defines the category each feature
(to group features) and another one with the variable to plot (this has to be

  - VALUE_FIELD: Value to use for the plot (Y axis). (Type: str)

Tool: Raster layer histogram
Algorithm ID: qgis:rasterlayerhistogram

Algorithm ID: qgis:vectorlayerhistogram

The attribute to use for computing the histogram must be numeric.

  - FIELD: Value to use for the plot (Y axis). (Type: str)
  - BINS: The number of bins to use in the histogram (X axis). Minimum 2. (Type: int) [Default: 10]
  - OUTPUT: Specify the HTML file for the plot. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **file_output_types** :end-before: **end_file_output_types** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Save to temporary file]``]

Toolbox: Point Cloud Conversion\nDescrip:
Tool: Convert format
Algorithm ID: pdal:convertformat
Description: Converts a point cloud to a different file format, e.g. creates a compressed :file:`.LAZ`.
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: Input point cloud layer to convert (Type: str)
  - OUTPUT: Specify the point cloud file to use as output. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **file_output_types** :end-before: **end_file_output_types** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Save to temporary file]``]

Tool: Export to raster
Algorithm ID: pdal:exportraster
Description: Exports point cloud data to a 2D raster grid having cell size of given resolution,
writing values from the specified attribute.
   Raster output using Intensity attribute of points
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: Input point cloud layer to export (Type: str)
  - ATTRIBUTE: A Field of the point cloud layer to extract the values from (Type: enum)
  - RESOLUTION: Cell size of the output raster (Type: float) [Default: 1.0]
  - TILE_SIZE: - (Type: int) [Default: 1000]
  - OUTPUT: Specify the raster file to export the data to. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **file_output_types** :end-before: **end_file_output_types** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Save to temporary file]``]

Tool: Export raster (using triangulation)
Algorithm ID: pdal:exportrastertin
Description: Exports point cloud data to a 2D raster grid using a triangulation of points
and then interpolating cell values from triangles.
.. note:: Using this algorithm can be slower if you are dealing with a large dataset.
   If your point cloud is dense, you can export your ground points as a raster using the :ref:`pdalexportraster` algorithm.
   Terrain raster output generated by point cloud triangulation
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: Input point cloud layer to export (Type: str)
  - RESOLUTION: Cell size of the output raster (Type: float) [Default: 1.0]
  - TILE_SIZE: - (Type: int) [Default: 1000]
  - OUTPUT: Specify the raster file to export the data to. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **file_output_types** :end-before: **end_file_output_types** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Save to temporary file]``]

Tool: Export to vector
Algorithm ID: pdal:exportvector
Description: Exports point cloud data to a vector layer with 3D points (a GeoPackage),
optionally with extra attributes.
   Exporting point cloud (ground points) to a vector layer styled based on the elevation
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: Input point cloud layer to export (Type: str)
  - OUTPUT: Specify the vector file to export the data to. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **file_output_types** :end-before: **end_file_output_types** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Save to temporary file]``]
Toolbox: Point Cloud Data Management\nDe:
Tool: Assign projection
Algorithm ID: pdal:assignprojection
Description: Assigns a Coordinate Reference System to a point cloud layer, if it is missing or wrong.
A new layer is created.
.. seealso:: :ref:`pdalreproject`
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: Input point cloud layer to assign a CRS to (Type: str)
  - CRS: The CRS to apply to the layer (Type: str)
  - OUTPUT: Specify the point cloud file to use as output. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **file_output_types** :end-before: **end_file_output_types** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Save to temporary file]``]

Tool: Build virtual point cloud (VPC)
Algorithm ID: pdal:virtualpointcloud
Description: Creates a :ref:`virtual point cloud (VPC) <virtual_point_cloud>` from input point cloud data.
If you leave the optional parameters unchecked, the VPC file will be built very quickly
as the algorithm will only read metadata of input files.
With any of the optional parameters set, the algorithm will read all points which can take some time.
   Generating Virtual Point Cloud with overview from a set of point cloud tiles
.. seealso:: :ref:`pdalmerge`
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - LAYERS: Input point cloud layers to combine inside a virtual point cloud layer (Type: list)
  - BOUNDARY: Set to True to show the exact boundaries of data (rather than just rectangular extent) (Type: bool) [Default: False]
  - STATISTICS: Set to True to understand ranges of values of the various attributes (Type: bool) [Default: False]
  - OVERVIEW: Generates a single “thinned” point cloud of all the input data (using only every 1000th point from original data). The overview point cloud will be created next to the VPC file - for example, for :file:`mydata.vpc`, the overview point cloud would be named :file:`mydata-overview.copc.laz`. (Type: bool) [Default: False]
  - OUTPUT: Specify the point cloud file to build the data into. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **file_output_types** :end-before: **end_file_output_types** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Save to temporary file]``]

Tool: Clip
Algorithm ID: pdal:clip
Description: Clips a point cloud layer by a polygon layer
so that the resulting point cloud contains only points within the polygons.
   Clipping an input point cloud layer with a polygon coverage
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: Input point cloud layer to clip (Type: str)
  - OVERLAY: Polygon vector layer to use as coverage for clipping the points (Type: str)
  - OUTPUT: Specify the point cloud file to export the clipped points to. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **file_output_types** :end-before: **end_file_output_types** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Save to temporary file]``]

Tool: Create COPC

Tool: Cell stack percent rank from value
Algorithm ID: native:cellstackpercentrankfromvalue
Description: Calculates the cell-wise percentrank value of a stack of rasters based on
a single input value and writes them to an output raster.
At each cell location, the specified value is ranked among the respective values
in the stack of all overlaid and sorted cell values from the input rasters.
For values outside of the stack value distribution, the algorithm returns NoData
because the value cannot be ranked among the cell values.
There are two methods for percentile calculation:
* Inclusive linear interpolation (PERCENTRANK.INC)
* Exclusive linear interpolation (PERCENTRANK.EXC)
The linear interpolation methods return the unique percent rank for different values.
Both interpolation methods follow their counterpart methods implemented
by `LibreOffice <https://help.libreoffice.org/latest/en-US/text/scalc/01/04060184.html?DbPAR=CALC#bm_id3148807>`_
or Microsoft Excel.
The output raster's extent and resolution is defined by a reference raster.
Input raster layers that do not match the cell size of the reference
raster layer will be resampled using nearest neighbor resampling.
NoData values in any of the input layers will result in a NoData cell output
if the "Ignore NoData values" parameter is not set.
The output raster data type will always be ``Float32``.
  Percent ranking Value = 1. ``NoData`` cells (grey) are ignored.
.. seealso:: :ref:`qgiscellstackpercentile`, :ref:`qgiscellstackpercentrankfromrasterlayer`
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: Raster layers to evaluate. If multiband rasters are used in the data raster stack, the algorithm will always perform the analysis on the first band of the rasters (Type: list)
  - METHOD: Method for percentile calculation: * 0 --- Inclusive linear interpolation (PERCENTRANK.INC) * 1 --- Exclusive linear interpolation (PERCENTRANK.EXC) (Type: enum) [Default: 0]
  - VALUE: Value to rank among the respective values in the stack of all overlaid and sorted cell values from the input rasters (Type: float) [Default: 10.0]
  - IGNORE_NODATA: If unchecked, any NoData cells in the input layers will result in a NoData cell in the output raster (Type: bool) [Default: True]
  - REFERENCE_LAYER: The reference layer for the output layer creation (extent, CRS, pixel dimensions) (Type: str)
  - OUTPUT: Specification of the output raster. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **file_output_types** :end-before: **end_file_output_types** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Save to temporary file]``]
Advanced Parameters:
  - OUTPUT_NODATA_VALUE: Value to use for NoData in the output layer (Type: float) [Default: -9999.0]

Tool: Cell stack percentile
Algorithm ID: native:cellstackpercentile
Description: Calculates the cell-wise percentile value of a stack of rasters
and writes the results to an output raster. The percentile to return
is determined by the percentile input value (ranges between 0 and 1).
At each cell location, the specified percentile is obtained using the respective
value from the stack of all overlaid and sorted cell values of the input rasters.
There are three methods for percentile calculation:
* Nearest rank: returns the value that is nearest to the specified percentile
* Inclusive linear interpolation (PERCENTRANK.INC)
* Exclusive linear interpolation (PERCENTRANK.EXC)
The linear interpolation methods return the unique values for different percentiles.
Both interpolation methods follow their counterpart methods implemented
by `LibreOffice <https://help.libreoffice.org/latest/en-US/text/scalc/01/04060184.html?DbPAR=CALC#bm_id3148807>`_
or Microsoft Excel.
The output raster's extent and resolution is defined by a reference raster.
Input raster layers that do not match the cell size of the reference
raster layer will be resampled using nearest neighbor resampling.
NoData values in any of the input layers will result in a NoData cell output
if the "Ignore NoData values" parameter is not set.
The output raster data type will always be ``Float32``.
  Percentile = 0.25. ``NoData`` cells (grey) are ignored.
.. seealso:: :ref:`qgiscellstackpercentile`, :ref:`qgiscellstackpercentrankfromrasterlayer`
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: Raster layers to evaluate. If multiband rasters are used in the data raster stack, the algorithm will always perform the analysis on the first band of the rasters (Type: list)
  - METHOD: Method for percentile calculation: * 0 --- Nearest rank: returns the value that is nearest to the specified percentile * 1 --- Inclusive linear interpolation (PERCENTILE.INC) * 2 --- Exclusive linear interpolation (PERCENTILE.EXC) (Type: enum) [Default: 0]
  - VALUE: Value to rank among the respective values in the stack of all overlaid and sorted cell values from the input rasters. Between 0 and 1. (Type: float) [Default: 0.25]
  - IGNORE_NODATA: If unchecked, any NoData cells in the input layers will result in a NoData cell in the output raster (Type: bool) [Default: True]
  - REFERENCE_LAYER: The reference layer for the output layer creation (extent, CRS, pixel dimensions) (Type: str)
  - OUTPUT: Specification of the output raster. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **file_output_types** :end-before: **end_file_output_types** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Save to temporary file]``]
Advanced Parameters:
  - OUTPUT_NODATA_VALUE: Value to use for NoData in the output layer (Type: float) [Default: -9999.0]

or Microsoft Excel.
The output raster's extent and resolution is defined by a reference raster.
Input raster layers that do not match the cell size of the reference
raster layer will be resampled using nearest neighbor resampling.
NoData values in any of the input layers will result in a NoData cell output
if the "Ignore NoData values" parameter is not set.

Tool: Cell statistics
Algorithm ID: native:cellstatistics
Description: Computes per-cell statistics based on input raster layers
and for each cell writes the resulting statistics to an output raster. At each
cell location, the output value is defined as a function of all overlaid
cell values of the input rasters.
By default, a NoData cell in ANY of the input layers will result in a
NoData cell in the output raster.
If the :guilabel:`Ignore NoData values` option is checked,
then NoData inputs will be ignored in the statistic calculation. This
may result in NoData output for locations where all cells are NoData.
The :guilabel:`Reference layer` parameter specifies an existing raster layer to
use as a reference when creating the output raster.
The output raster will have the same extent, CRS, and pixel dimensions
as this layer.
**Calculation details:**
Input raster layers that do not match the cell size of the reference
raster layer will be resampled using ``nearest neighbor resampling``.
The output raster data type will be set to the most complex
data type present in the input datasets except when using the
functions ``Mean``, ``Standard deviation`` and ``Variance`` (data type is always
``Float32`` or ``Float64`` depending on input float type) or ``Count``
and ``Variety`` (data type is always ``Int32``).
- ``Count``: The count statistic will always result in the number of cells
  without NoData values at the current cell location.
- ``Median``: If the number of input layers is even, the median will be
  calculated as the arithmetic mean of the two middle values of the ordered cell input values.
- ``Minority/Majority``: If no unique minority or majority could be found,
  the result is NoData, except all input cell values are equal.
  Example with all the statistic functions. ``NoData`` cells (grey) are taken into account.
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: Input raster layers (Type: list)
  - STATISTIC: Available statistics. Options: * 0 --- Sum * 1 --- Count * 2 --- Mean * 3 --- Median * 4 --- Standard deviation * 5 --- Variance * 6 --- Minimum * 7 --- Maximum * 8 --- Minority (least common value) * 9 --- Majority (most common value) * 10 --- Range (max - min) * 11 --- Variety (unique value count) (Type: enum) [Default: 0]
  - IGNORE_NODATA: Calculate statistics also for all cells stacks, ignoring NoData occurrence. (Type: bool) [Default: True]
  - REF_LAYER: The reference layer to create the output layer from (extent, CRS, pixel dimensions) (Type: str)
  - OUTPUT: Specification of the output raster. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **file_output_types** :end-before: **end_file_output_types** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Save to temporary file]``]

Tool: Equal to frequency
Algorithm ID: native:equaltofrequency
Description: Evaluates on a cell-by-cell basis the frequency (number of times) the values
of an input stack of rasters are equal to the value of a value layer.
The output raster extent and resolution are defined by the input raster layer
and is always of ``Int32`` type.
If multiband rasters are used in the data raster stack, the algorithm will always
perform the analysis on the first band of the rasters - use GDAL to use other bands
in the analysis.
The output NoData value can be set manually.
  For each cell in the output raster, the value represents the number of times
  that the corresponding cells in the list of rasters are the same as the value raster.
  ``NoData`` cells (grey) are taken into account.
.. **frequencyparams**
.. FYI, the next params description is shared with Greater/Less than frequency algorithms
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT_VALUE_RASTER: The input value layer serves as reference layer for the sample layers (Type: str)
  - INPUT_VALUE_RASTER_BAND: Select the band you want to use as sample (Type: str) [Default: The first band of the raster layer]
  - INPUT_RASTERS: Raster layers to evaluate. If multiband rasters are used in the data raster stack, the algorithm will always perform the analysis on the first band of the rasters (Type: list)
  - IGNORE_NODATA: If unchecked, any NoData cells in the value raster or the data layer stack will result in a NoData cell in the output raster (Type: bool) [Default: False]
  - OUTPUT: Specification of the output raster. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **file_output_types** :end-before: **end_file_output_types** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Save to temporary file]``]

Tool: Fuzzify raster (gaussian membership)
Algorithm ID: native:fuzzifyrastergaussianmembership
Description: Transforms an input raster to a fuzzified raster by assigning a
membership value to each pixel, using a Gaussian membership function.
Membership values range from 0 to 1.
In the fuzzified raster, a value of 0 implies no membership of the
defined fuzzy set, whereas a value of 1 means full membership.
The gaussian membership function is defined as |gaussian_formula|,
where *f1* is the spread and *f2* the midpoint.
  Fuzzify raster example. Input raster source: Land Tirol -
  data.tirol.gv.at.

  :ref:`qgisfuzzifyrasternearmembership`,
  :ref:`qgisfuzzifyrasterpowermembership`,

Tool: Fuzzify raster (linear membership)
Algorithm ID: native:fuzzifyrasterlinearmembership
Description: Transforms an input raster to a fuzzified raster by assigning a
membership value to each pixel, using a Linear membership function.
Membership values range from 0 to 1. In the fuzzified raster, a value
of 0 implies no membership of the defined fuzzy set, whereas a value
of 1 means full membership.
The linear function is defined as |fuzzy_linear_formula|, where *a*
is the low bound and *b* the high bound. This equation assigns
membership values using a linear transformation for pixel values
between the low and high bounds.
Pixels values smaller than the low bound are given 0 membership
whereas pixel values greater than the high bound are given 1
membership.

Tool: Raster boolean AND
Algorithm ID: native:rasterbooleanand
Description: Calculates the boolean ``AND`` for a set of input rasters.
If all of the input rasters have a non-zero value for a pixel, that
pixel will be set to ``1`` in the output raster.
If any of the input rasters have ``0`` values for the pixel it will
be set to ``0`` in the output raster.
The reference layer parameter specifies an existing raster layer to
use as a reference when creating the output raster.
The output raster will have the same extent, CRS, and pixel dimensions
as this layer.
By default, a NoData pixel in ANY of the input layers will result in a
NoData pixel in the output raster.
If the :guilabel:`Treat NoData values as false` option is checked,
then NoData inputs will be treated the same as a ``0`` input value.
.. seealso:: :ref:`qgisrasterbooleanor`

  - INPUT: List of input raster layers (Type: list)
  - REF_LAYER: The reference layer to create the output layer from (extent, CRS, pixel dimensions) (Type: str)
  - NODATA_AS_FALSE: Treat NoData values in the input files as 0 when performing the operation (Type: bool) [Default: False]
  - OUTPUT: Specification of the output raster containing the result. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **file_output_types** :end-before: **end_file_output_types** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Save to temporary file]``]

Tool: Raster calculator (virtual)

Description: Performs algebraic operations using raster layers and generates in-memory result.
The resulting layer will have its values computed according to an expression.
The expression can contain numerical values, operators and references
to any of the layers in the current project.
A virtual raster layer is a raster layer defined by its URI and whose pixels are calculated on-the-fly.
It's not a new file on disk; the virtual layer is still connected to the rasters used in the calculation
meaning that deleting or moving these rasters would break it.
A :guilabel:`Layer name` can be provided, otherwise the calculation expression is used as such.
Removing the virtual layer from the project deletes it, and it can be made persistent in file using the layer

Tool: Round raster
Algorithm ID: native:roundrastervalues
Description: Rounds the cell values of a raster dataset according to the specified number of decimals.
Alternatively, a negative number of decimal places may be used to round values
to powers of a base n. For example, with a Base value n of 10 and Decimal places
of -1, the algorithm rounds cell values to multiples of 10,
-2 rounds to multiples of 100, and so on.
Arbitrary base values may be chosen, the algorithm applies the same multiplicative
principle. Rounding cell values to multiples of a base n may be used to generalize
raster layers.
The algorithm preserves the data type of the input raster. Therefore byte/integer
rasters can only be rounded to multiples of a base n, otherwise a warning is raised
and the raster gets copied as byte/integer raster.
  Rounding values of a raster
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: The raster to process. (Type: str)
  - BAND: The band of the raster (Type: int) [Default: 1]
  - ROUNDING_DIRECTION: How to choose the target rounded value. Options are: * 0 --- Round up * 1 --- Round to nearest * 2 --- Round down (Type: list) [Default: 1]
  - DECIMAL_PLACES: Number of decimals places to round to. Use negative values to round cell values to a multiple of a base n (Type: int) [Default: 2]

Tool: Aspect
Algorithm ID: qgis:aspect
Description: Calculates the aspect of the Digital Terrain Model in input.
The final aspect raster layer contains values from 0 to 360 that
express the slope direction, starting from north (0°) and continuing
clockwise.
   Aspect values
The following picture shows the aspect layer reclassified with a color
ramp:
   Aspect layer reclassified
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: Digital Terrain Model raster layer (Type: str)
  - Z_FACTOR: Vertical exaggeration. This parameter is useful when the Z units differ from the X and Y units, for example feet and meters. You can use this parameter to adjust for this. The default is 1 (no exaggeration). (Type: float) [Default: 1.0]
  - OUTPUT: Specify the output aspect raster layer. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **file_output_types** :end-before: **end_file_output_types** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Save to temporary file]``]

Tool: based)
Algorithm ID: native:dtmslopebasedfilter
Description: Can be used to filter a digital elevation model in order to classify its cells into ground and object (non-ground) cells.
The tool uses concepts as described by Vosselman (2000)
and is based on the assumption that a large height difference between two nearby cells is unlikely to be caused by a steep slope in the terrain.
The probability that the higher cell might be non-ground increases when the distance between the two cells decreases.
Therefore the filter defines a maximum height difference (``dz_max``) between two cells as a function of the distance (``d``) between the cells (``dz_max( d ) = d``).
A cell is classified as terrain if there is no cell within the kernel radius
to which the height difference is larger than the allowed maximum height difference at the distance between these two cells.
The approximate terrain slope (``s``) parameter is used to modify the filter function
to match the overall slope in the study area (``dz_max( d ) = d * s``).
A 5 % confidence interval (``ci = 1.65 * sqrt( 2 * stddev )``) may be used to modify the filter function even further
by either relaxing (``dz_max( d ) = d * s + ci``) or amplifying (``dz_max( d ) = d * s - ci``) the filter criterium.
*References: Vosselman, G. (2000): Slope based filtering of laser altimetry data. IAPRS, Vol. XXXIII, Part B3, Amsterdam, The Netherlands, 935-942*
.. seealso:: This tool is a port of the SAGA `DTM Filter (slope-based) <https://saga-gis.sourceforge.io/saga_tool_doc/9.1.1/grid_filter_7.html>`_
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: Digital Terrain Model raster layer (Type: str)
  - BAND: The band of the DEM to consider (Type: float)
  - RADIUS: The radius of the filter kernel (in pixels). Must be large enough to reach ground cells next to non-ground objects. (Type: int) [Default: 5]
  - TERRAIN_SLOPE: The approximate terrain slope in ``%``. The terrain slope must be adjusted to account for the ratio of height units vs raster pixel dimensions. Used to relax the filter criterium in steeper terrain. (Type: int) [Default: 30]
  - FILTER_MODIFICATION: Choose whether to apply the filter kernel without modification or to use a confidence interval to relax or amplify the height criterium. * 0 - None * 1 - Relax filter * 2 - Amplify (Type: list) [Default: 0]
  - STANDARD_DEVIATION: The standard deviation used to calculate a 5% confidence interval applied to the height threshold. (Type: float) [Default: 0.1]

Tool: Hillshade
Algorithm ID: qgis:hillshade
Description: Calculates the hillshade raster layer given an input Digital Terrain
Model.
The shading of the layer is calculated according to the sun position:
you have the options to change both the horizontal angle (azimuth) and
the vertical angle (sun elevation) of the sun.
   Azimuth and vertical angle
The hillshade layer contains values from 0 (complete shadow) to 255
(complete sun).
Hillshade is used usually to better understand the relief of the area.
   Hillshade layer with azimuth 300 and vertical angle 45
Particularly interesting is to give the hillshade layer a transparency
value and overlap it with the elevation raster:
   Overlapping the hillshade with the elevation layer
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: Digital Terrain Model raster layer (Type: str)
  - Z_FACTOR: Vertical exaggeration. This parameter is useful when the Z units differ from the X and Y units, for example feet and meters. You can use this parameter to adjust for this. Increasing the value of this parameter will exaggerate the final result (making it look more "hilly"). The default is 1 (no exaggeration). (Type: float) [Default: 1.0]
  - AZIMUTH: Set the horizontal angle (in degrees) of the sun (clockwise direction). Range: 0 to 360. 0 is north. (Type: float) [Default: 300.0]
  - V_ANGLE: Set the vertical angle (in degrees) of the sun, that is the height of the sun. Values can go from 0 (minimum elevation) to 90 (maximum elevation). (Type: float) [Default: 40.0]
  - OUTPUT: Specify the output hillshade raster layer. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **file_output_types** :end-before: **end_file_output_types** (Type: str) [Default: ``Save to temporary file``]

Tool: Hypsometric curves
Algorithm ID: qgis:hypsometriccurves
Description: Calculates hypsometric curves for an input Digital Elevation Model.
Curves are produced as CSV files in an output folder specified by the
user.
A hypsometric curve is a cumulative histogram of elevation values in
a geographical area.
You can use hypsometric curves to detect differences in the landscape
due to the geomorphology of the territory.
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT_DEM: Digital Terrain Model raster layer to use for calculating altitudes (Type: str)
  - BOUNDARY_LAYER: Polygon vector layer with boundaries of areas used to calculate hypsometric curves (Type: str)
  - STEP: Vertical distance between curves (Type: float) [Default: 100.0]
  - USE_PERCENTAGE: Write area percentage to “Area” field of the CSV file instead of the absolute area (Type: bool) [Default: False]
  - OUTPUT_DIRECTORY: Specify the output folder for the hypsometric curves. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **directory_output_types** :end-before: **end_directory_output_types** (Type: str)

Description: Creates a shaded relief layer from digital elevation data.
You can specify the relief color manually, or you can let the

Increasing the value of this parameter will exaggerate the final result (making it look more "hilly"). The default is 1 (no exaggeration). (Type: float) [Default: 1.0]
  - AUTO_COLORS: If you check this option the algorithm will create all the relief color classes automatically (Type: bool) [Default: False]

Tool: Ruggedness index
Algorithm ID: qgis:ruggednessindex
Description: Calculates the quantitative measurement of terrain heterogeneity
described by Riley et al. (1999).
It is calculated for every location, by summarizing the change in
elevation within the 3x3 pixel grid.
Each pixel contains the difference in elevation from a center cell and
the 8 cells surrounding it.
   Ruggedness layer from low (red) to high values (green)
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: Digital Terrain Model raster layer (Type: str)
  - Z_FACTOR: Vertical exaggeration. This parameter is useful when the Z units differ from the X and Y units, for example feet and meters. You can use this parameter to adjust for this. Increasing the value of this parameter will exaggerate the final result (making it look more rugged). The default is 1 (no exaggeration). (Type: float) [Default: 1.0]
  - OUTPUT: Specify the output ruggedness raster layer. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **file_output_types** :end-before: **end_file_output_types** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Save to temporary file]``]

Tool: Slope
Algorithm ID: qgis:slope
Description: Calculates the slope from an input raster layer. The slope is the
angle of inclination of the terrain and is expressed in **degrees**.
   Flat areas in red, steep areas in blue
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: Digital Terrain Model raster layer (Type: str)

Increasing the value of this parameter will exaggerate the final result (making it steeper). The default is 1 (no exaggeration). (Type: float) [Default: 1.0]
  - OUTPUT: Specify the output slope raster layer. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **file_output_types** :end-before: **end_file_output_types** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Save to temporary file]``]

Tool: Climb along line
Algorithm ID: qgis:climbalongline
Description: Calculates the total climb and descent along line geometries.
The input layer must have Z values present. If Z values are not
available, the  :ref:`qgissetzfromraster` algorithm may be used to add
Z values from a DEM layer.
The output layer is a copy of the input layer with additional fields
that contain the total climb (``climb``), total descent (``descent``),
the minimum elevation (``minelev``) and the maximum elevation
(``maxelev``) for each line geometry.
If the input layer contains fields with the same names as these added
fields, they will be renamed (field names will be altered to "name_2",
"name_3", etc, finding the first non-duplicate name).
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: Line layer to calculate the climb for. Must have Z values (Type: str)
  - OUTPUT: Specification of the output (line) layer. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **layer_output_types** :end-before: **end_layer_output_types** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Create temporary layer]``]

Tool: Count points in polygon

points count corresponding to each polygon.
  The labels in the polygons show the point count
An optional weight field can be used to assign weights to each point.
Alternatively, a unique class field can be specified.
If both options are used, the weight field will take precedence and
the unique class field will be ignored.

of polygon features

Parameters:

  - OUTPUT: Specification of the output layer. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **layer_output_types_append** :end-before: **end_layer_output_types_append** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Create temporary layer]``]

Tool: Distance matrix
Algorithm ID: qgis:distancematrix
Description: Calculates for point features distances to their nearest features in
the same layer or in another layer.
.. seealso:: :ref:`qgisjoinbynearest`
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: Point layer for which the distance matrix is calculated (**from** points) (Type: str)
  - INPUT_FIELD: Field to use to uniquely identify features of the input layer. Used in the output attribute table. (Type: str)
  - TARGET: Point layer containing the nearest point(s) to search (**to** points) (Type: str)
  - TARGET_FIELD: Field to use to uniquely identify features of the target layer. Used in the output attribute table. (Type: str)
  - MATRIX_TYPE: Different types of calculation are available: * 0 --- Linear (N * *k* x 3) distance matrix: for each input point, reports the distance to each of the *k* nearest target points. The output matrix consists of up to *k* rows per input point, and each row has three columns: *InputID*, *TargetID* and *Distance*. * 1 --- Standard (N x T) distance matrix * 2 --- Summary distance matrix (mean, std. dev., min, max): for each input point, reports statistics on the distances to its target points. (Type: enum) [Default: 0]
  - NEAREST_POINTS: You can choose to calculate the distance to all the points in the target layer (*0*) or limit to a number (*k*) of closest features. (Type: int) [Default: 0]
  - OUTPUT: Specification of the output vector layer. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **layer_output_types** :end-before: **end_layer_output_types** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Create temporary layer]``]

Tool: Distance to nearest hub (line to hub)

Description: Creates lines that join each feature of an input vector to the nearest

  - UNIT: Units in which to report the distance to the closest feature: * 0 --- Meters * 1 --- Feet * 2 --- Miles * 3 --- Kilometers * 4 --- Layer units (Type: enum) [Default: 0]
  - OUTPUT: Specify the output line vector layer connecting the matching points. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **layer_output_types** :end-before: **end_layer_output_types** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Create temporary layer]``]

Tool: Distance to nearest hub (points)
Algorithm ID: qgis:distancetonearesthubpoints
Description: Creates a point layer representing the
:ref:`center <qgispointonsurface>` of the input features with the
addition of two fields containing the identifier of the nearest

points.
   :ref:`qgisjoinbynearest`
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: Vector layer for which the nearest feature is searched (Type: str)
  - HUBS: Vector layer containing the features to search for (Type: str)
  - FIELD: Field to use to uniquely identify features of the destination layer. Used in the output attribute table (Type: str)
  - UNIT: Units in which to report the distance to the closest feature: * 0 --- Meters * 1 --- Feet * 2 --- Miles * 3 --- Kilometers * 4 --- Layer units (Type: enum) [Default: 0]

Tool: Join by lines (hub lines)
Algorithm ID: native:hublines
Description: Creates hub and spoke diagrams by connecting lines from points on
the Spoke layer to matching points in the Hub layer.
Determination of which hub goes with each point is based on a match
between the Hub ID field on the hub points and the Spoke ID field on
the spoke points.
If input layers are not point layers, a point on the surface of the
geometries will be taken as the connecting location.
Optionally, geodesic lines can be created, which represent the
shortest path on the surface of an ellipsoid.
When geodesic mode is used, it is possible to split the created lines
at the antimeridian (±180 degrees longitude), which can improve
rendering of the lines.
Additionally, the distance between vertices can be specified.
A smaller distance results in a denser, more accurate line.
  Join points based on a common field / attribute
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - HUBS: Input layer (Type: str)
  - HUB_FIELD: Field of the hub layer with ID to join (Type: str)
  - SPOKES: Additional spoke point layer (Type: str)
  - SPOKE_FIELD: Field of the spoke layer with ID to join (Type: str)
  - GEODESIC: Create geodesic lines (the shortest path on the surface of an ellipsoid) (Type: bool) [Default: False]
  - OUTPUT: Specify the output hub line vector layer. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **layer_output_types** :end-before: **end_layer_output_types** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Create temporary layer]``]
Advanced Parameters:
  - GEODESIC_DISTANCE: Distance between consecutive vertices (in kilometers). A smaller distance results in a denser, more accurate line (Type: float) [Default: 1000.0 (kilometers)]
  - ANTIMERIDIAN_SPLIT: Split lines at ±180 degrees longitude (to improve rendering of the lines) (Type: bool) [Default: False]

Tool: means clustering
Algorithm ID: native:kmeansclustering
Description: Calculates the 2D distance based k-means cluster number for each input
feature.
K-means clustering aims to partition the features into k clusters in
which each feature belongs to the cluster with the nearest mean.
The mean point is represented by the barycenter of the clustered
features.
If input geometries are lines or polygons, the clustering is based on
the centroid of the feature.
  A five class point clusters
.. seealso:: :ref:`qgisdbscanclustering`, :ref:`qgisstdbscanclustering`
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: Layer to analyze (Type: str)
  - CLUSTERS: Number of clusters to create with the features (Type: int) [Default: 5]
  - OUTPUT: Specify the output vector layer for generated the clusters. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **layer_output_types** :end-before: **end_layer_output_types** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Create temporary layer]``]
Advanced Parameters:
  - FIELD_NAME: Name of the field where the associated cluster number shall be stored (Type: str) [Default: 'CLUSTER_ID']
  - SIZE_FIELD_NAME: Name of the field with the count of features in the same cluster (Type: str) [Default: 'CLUSTER_SIZE']

Algorithm ID: native:meancoordinates
Description: Computes a point layer with the center of mass of geometries in an

An attribute can be specified as containing weights to be applied to

If an attribute is selected in the parameter, features will be grouped
according to values in this field.
Instead of a single point with the center of mass of the whole layer,
the output layer will contain a center of mass for the features in

Tool: Nearest neighbour analysis
Algorithm ID: native:nearestneighbouranalysis
Description: Performs nearest neighbor analysis for a point layer. The output tells you
how your data are distributed (clustered, randomly or distributed).
Output is generated as an HTML file with the computed statistical
values:
* Observed mean distance
* Expected mean distance
* Nearest neighbour index
* Number of points
* Z-Score: Comparing the Z-Score with the normal distribution tells
  you how your data are distributed.
  A low Z-Score means that the data are unlikely to be the result of a
  spatially random process, while a high Z-Score means that your data
  are likely to be a result of a spatially random process.
.. seealso:: :ref:`qgisjoinbynearest`
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: Point vector layer to calculate the statistics on (Type: str)

Tool: Overlap analysis
Algorithm ID: native:calculatevectoroverlaps
Description: Calculates the area and percentage cover by which features from an
input layer are overlapped by features from a selection of overlay
layers.
New attributes are added to the output layer reporting the
total area of overlap and percentage of the input feature
overlapped by each of the selected overlay layers.
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: The input layer. (Type: str)
  - LAYERS: The overlay layers. (Type: list)
  - OUTPUT: Specify the output vector layer. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **layer_output_types** :end-before: **end_layer_output_types** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Create temporary layer]``]

Tool: Shortest line between features
Algorithm ID: native:shortestline
Description: Creates a line layer as the shortest line between the source and the destination layer. By default only the first nearest feature of the destination layer is taken into account. The n-nearest neighboring features number can be specified.
If a maximum distance is specified, then only features which are closer than this distance will be considered.
The output features will contain all the source layer attributes, all the attributes from the n-nearest feature and the additional field of the distance.
.. important:: This algorithm uses purely Cartesian calculations for distance,
  and does not consider geodetic or ellipsoid properties when determining
  feature proximity. The measurement and output coordinate system is based
  on the coordinate system of the source layer.
   Shortest line from point features to lines
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - SOURCE: Origin layer for which to search for nearest neighbors (Type: str)
  - DESTINATION: Target Layer in which to search for nearest neighbors (Type: str)
  - METHOD: Shortest distance calculation method Possible values are: * 0 --- Distance to nearest point on feature * 1 --- Distance to feature centroid (Type: enum) [Default: 0]
  - NEIGHBORS: Maximum number of neighbors to look for (Type: int) [Default: 1]
  - OUTPUT: Specify the output vector layer. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **layer_output_types** :end-before: **end_layer_output_types** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Create temporary layer]``]

Tool: Array of offset (parallel) lines
Algorithm ID: native:arrayoffsetlines
Description: Creates copies of line features in a layer, by creating multiple
offset versions of each feature.
Each new version is incrementally offset by a specified distance.
Positive distance will offset lines to the left, and negative
distances will offset them to the right.
   In blue the source layer, in red the offset one
of line features
.. seealso:: :ref:`qgisoffsetline`, :ref:`qgisarraytranslatedfeatures`
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: Input line vector layer to use for the offsets. (Type: str)
  - COUNT: Number of offset copies to generate for each feature (Type: int) [Default: 10]
  - OFFSET: Distance between two consecutive offset copies (Type: float) [Default: 1.0]

Advanced Parameters:

  - JOIN_STYLE: Specify whether round, miter or beveled joins should be used when offsetting corners in a line. One of: * 0 --- Round * 1 --- Miter * 2 --- Bevel Round, miter, and bevel join styles (Type: enum) [Default: 0]
  - MITER_LIMIT: Sets the maximum distance from the offset geometry to use when creating a mitered join as a factor of the offset distance (only applicable for miter join styles). Minimum: 1.0 A 10m buffer with a limit of 2 and a 10m buffer with a limit of 1 (Type: float) [Default: 2.0]

Tool: Random points along line
Algorithm ID: qgis:qgisrandompointsalongline
Description: Creates a new point layer, with points placed on the lines of another
layer.
For each line in the input layer, a given number of points is added
to the resulting layer.
The procedure for adding a point is to:
1. randomly select a line feature from the input layer
2. if the feature is multi-part, randomly select a part of it
3. randomly select a segment of that line
4. randomly select a position on that segment.
The procedure means that curved parts of the lines (with relatively
short segments) will get more points than straight parts (with
relatively long segments), as demonstrated in the illustration below,
where the output of the *Random points along lines* algorithm can be
compared with the output of the *Random points on lines* algorithm
(that produces points with an, on average, even distribution along
the lines).
   Example algorithm output. Left: *Random points along line*, right:
   *Random points on lines*
A minimum distance can be specified, to avoid points being too close
to each other.
.. seealso:: :ref:`qgisrandompointsonlines`
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: Input line vector layer (Type: str)
  - POINTS_NUMBER: Number of points to create (Type: int) [Default: 1]
  - MIN_DISTANCE: The minimum distance between points (Type: float) [Default: 0.0]
  - OUTPUT: The output random points. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **layer_output_types** :end-before: **end_layer_output_types** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Create temporary layer]``]
