  - MAX_ATTEMPTS: Maximum number of attempts to place the points (Type: int) [Default: 200]

Tool: Random points in layer bounds
Algorithm ID: qgis:randompointsinlayerbounds
Description: Creates a new point layer with a given number of random points,
all of them within the extent of a given layer.
A minimum distance can be specified, to avoid points being too
close to each other.
**Default menu**: :menuselection:`Vector --> Research Tools`
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: Input polygon layer defining the area (Type: str)
  - POINTS_NUMBER: Number of points to create (Type: int) [Default: 1]
  - MIN_DISTANCE: The minimum distance between points (Type: float) [Default: 0.0]
  - OUTPUT: The output random points. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **layer_output_types** :end-before: **end_layer_output_types** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Create temporary layer]``]

Tool: Random points in polygons
Algorithm ID: native:randompointsinpolygons
Description: Creates a point layer with points placed inside the polygons of
another layer.
For each feature (polygon / multi-polygon) geometry in the input
layer, the given number of points is added to the result layer.
Per feature and global minimum distances can be specified in order to
avoid points being too close in the output point layer.
If a minimum distance is specified, it may not be possible to generate
the specified number of points for each feature.
The total number of generated points and missed points are available
as output from the algorithm.
The illustration below shows the effect of per feature and global
minimum distances and zero/non-zero minimum distances (generated with
the same seed, so at least the first point generated will be the
same).
   Ten points per polygon feature, *left*: min. distances = 0,
   *middle*: min.distances = 1, *right*: min. distance = 1,
   global min. distance = 0
The maximum number of tries per point can be specified.
This is only relevant for non-zero minimum distance.
A seed for the random number generator can be provided, making it
possible to get identical random number sequences for different runs
of the algorithm.
The attributes of the polygon feature on which a point was generated
can be included (:guilabel:`Include polygon attributes`).
If you want approximately the same point density for all the
features, you can data-define the number of points using the area of
the polygon feature geometry.
.. seealso:: :ref:`qgisrandompointsinsidepolygons`
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: Input polygon vector layer (Type: str)
  - POINTS_NUMBER: Number of points to create (Type: int) [Default: 1]
  - OUTPUT: The output random points. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **layer_output_types** :end-before: **end_layer_output_types** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Create temporary layer]``]
Advanced Parameters:
  - INCLUDE_POLYGON_ATTRIBUTES: If set, a point will get the attributes from the line on which it is placed. (Type: bool) [Default: True]

Tool: Random points inside polygons
Algorithm ID: qgis:randompointsinsidepolygons
Description: Creates a new point layer with a given number of random points
inside each polygon of the input polygon layer.
Two sampling strategies are available:
* Points count: number of points for each feature
* Points density: density of points for each feature
A minimum distance can be specified, to avoid points being too close
to each other.
.. seealso:: :ref:`qgisrandompointsinpolygons`
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: Input polygon vector layer (Type: str)
  - STRATEGY: Sampling strategy to use. One of: * 0 --- Points count: number of points for each feature * 1 --- Points density: density of points for each feature (Type: enum) [Default: 0]
  - VALUE: The number or density of points, depending on the chosen :guilabel:`Sampling strategy`. (Type: float) [Default: 1.0]
  - MIN_DISTANCE: The minimum distance between points (Type: float) [Default: 0.0]
  - OUTPUT: The output random points. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **layer_output_types** :end-before: **end_layer_output_types** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Create temporary layer]``]

Tool: Random points on lines
Algorithm ID: native:randompointsonlines
Description: Creates a point layer with points placed on the lines of another
layer.
For each feature (line / multi-line) geometry in the input layer, the
given number of points is added to the result layer.
Per feature and global minimum distances can be specified in order to
avoid points being too close in the output point layer.
If a minimum distance is specified, it may not be possible to generate
the specified number of points for each feature.
The total number of generated points and missed points are available
as output from the algorithm.
The illustration below shows the effect of per feature and global
minimum distances and zero/non-zero minimum distances (generated with
the same seed, so at least the first point generated will be the
same).
   Five points per line feature, *left*: min. distances = 0,
   *middle*: min.distances != 0, *right*: min. distance != 0,
   global min. distance = 0
The maximum number of tries per point can be specified.
This is only relevant for non-zero minimum distance.
A seed for the random number generator can be provided, making it
possible to get identical random number sequences for different runs
of the algorithm.
The attributes of the line feature on which a point was generated can
be included (:guilabel:`Include line attributes`).
If you want approximately the same point density for all the line
features, you can data-define the number of points using the length of
the line feature geometry.
.. seealso:: :ref:`qgisrandompointsalongline`
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: Input line vector layer (Type: str)
  - POINTS_NUMBER: Number of points to create (Type: int) [Default: 1]
  - OUTPUT: The output random points. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **layer_output_types** :end-before: **end_layer_output_types** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Create temporary layer]``]
Advanced Parameters:
  - INCLUDE_LINE_ATTRIBUTES: If set, a point will get the attributes from the line on which it is placed. (Type: bool) [Default: True]

Tool: Raster pixels to points
Algorithm ID: native:pixelstopoints
Description: Creates a vector layer of points corresponding to each pixel in a
raster layer.
Converts a raster layer to a vector layer, by creating point features
for each individual pixel's center in the raster layer.
Any NoData  pixels are skipped in the output.
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT_RASTER: Input raster layer (Type: str)
  - RASTER_BAND: Raster band to extract data from (Type: str)
  - FIELD_NAME: Name of the field to store the raster band value (Type: str) [Default: 'VALUE']
  - OUTPUT: Specify the resulting point layer of pixels centroids. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **layer_output_types** :end-before: **end_layer_output_types** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Create temporary layer]``]

Tool: Raster pixels to polygons
Algorithm ID: native:pixelstopolygons
Description: Creates a vector layer of polygons corresponding to each pixel in a
raster layer.
Converts a raster layer to a vector layer, by creating polygon
features for each individual pixel's extent in the raster layer.
Any NoData  pixels are skipped in the output.
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT_RASTER: Input raster layer (Type: str)
  - RASTER_BAND: Raster band to extract data from (Type: str)
  - FIELD_NAME: Name of the field to store the raster band value (Type: str) [Default: 'VALUE']
  - OUTPUT: Specify the resulting polygon layer of pixel extents. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **layer_output_types** :end-before: **end_layer_output_types** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Create temporary layer]``]

Tool: Regular points
Algorithm ID: qgis:regularpoints
Description: Creates a new point layer with its points placed in a regular grid
within a given extent.
The grid is specified either by the spacing between the points (same
spacing for all dimensions) or by the number of points to generate.
In the latter case, the spacing will be determined from the extent.
In order to generate a full rectangular grid, at least the number of
points specified by the user is generated for the latter case.
Random offsets to the point spacing can be applied, resulting in a
non-regular point pattern.
**Default menu**: :menuselection:`Vector --> Research Tools`
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - EXTENT: Map extent for the random points .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **extent_options** :end-before: **end_extent_options** (Type: str)
  - SPACING: Spacing between the points, or the number of points, depending on whether ``Use point spacing`` is checked or not. (Type: int) [Default: 100]
  - INSET: Offsets the points relative to the upper left corner. The value is used for both the X and Y axis. (Type: float) [Default: 0.0]
  - RANDOMIZE: If checked the points will have a random spacing (Type: bool) [Default: False]
  - IS_SPACING: If unchecked the point spacing is not taken into account (Type: bool) [Default: True]
  - CRS: CRS of the random points layer (Type: str) [Default: *Project CRS*]
  - OUTPUT: Specify the output regular point layer. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **layer_output_types** :end-before: **end_layer_output_types** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Create temporary layer]``]
Toolbox: Vector general\nDescription: Th:
Tool: Assign projection
Algorithm ID: native:assignprojection
Description: Assigns a new projection to a vector layer.
It creates a new layer with the exact same features and geometries as
the input one, but assigned to a new CRS. The geometries are **not**
reprojected, they are just assigned to a different CRS.
This algorithm can be used to repair layers which have been assigned
an incorrect projection.
Attributes are not modified by this algorithm.
   :ref:`qgisfindprojection`, :ref:`qgisreprojectlayer`
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: Vector layer with wrong or missing CRS (Type: str)
  - CRS: Select the new CRS to assign to the vector layer (Type: str) [Default: ``EPSG:4326 - WGS84``]

Tool: Batch Nominatim geocoder
Algorithm ID: native:batchnominatimgeocoder
Description: Performs batch geocoding using the Nominatim service against an input
layer string field.
The output layer will have a point geometry reflecting the geocoded location
as well as a number of attributes associated to the geocoded location.
:ref:`features in-place modification <processing_inplace_edit>` 
of point features
.. note:: This algorithm is compliant with the `usage policy
 <https://operations.osmfoundation.org/policies/nominatim/>`_ of the
 Nominatim geocoding service provided by the OpenStreetMap Foundation.
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: Vector layer to geocode the features (Type: str)
  - FIELD: Field containing the addresses to geocode (Type: str)
  - OUTPUT: Specify the output layer containing only the geocoded addresses. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **layer_output_types_append** :end-before: **end_layer_output_types_append** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Create temporary layer]``]

Tool: Convert layer to spatial bookmarks
Algorithm ID: native:layertobookmarks
Description: Creates spatial bookmarks corresponding to the extent of features
contained in a layer.
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: The input vector layer (Type: str)
  - DESTINATION: Select the destination for the bookmarks. One of: * 0 --- Project bookmarks * 1 --- User bookmarks (Type: enum) [Default: 0]
  - NAME_EXPRESSION: Field or expression that will give names to the generated bookmarks (Type: str)
  - GROUP_EXPRESSION: Field or expression that will provide groups for the generated bookmarks (Type: str)

Tool: Convert spatial bookmarks to layer
Algorithm ID: native:bookmarkstolayer
Description: Creates a new layer containing polygon features for stored spatial
bookmarks.
The export can be filtered to only bookmarks belonging to the current
project, to all user bookmarks, or a combination of both.
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - SOURCE: Select the source(s) of the bookmarks. One or more of: * 0 --- Project bookmarks * 1 --- User bookmarks (Type: enum) [Default: [0,1]]
  - CRS: The CRS of the output layer (Type: str) [Default: ``EPSG:4326 - WGS 84``]
  - OUTPUT: Specify the output layer. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **layer_output_types** :end-before: **end_layer_output_types** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Create temporary layer]``]

Tool: Create attribute index
Algorithm ID: native:createattributeindex
Description: Creates an index against a field of the attribute table to speed up
queries.
The support for index creation depends on both the layer's data
provider and the field type.
No outputs are created: the index is stored on the layer itself.
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: Select the vector layer you want to create an attribute index for (Type: str)
  - FIELD: Field of the vector layer (Type: str)

Tool: Create spatial index
Algorithm ID: native:createspatialindex
Description: Creates an index to speed up access to the features in a layer based
on their spatial location.
Support for spatial index creation is dependent on the layer's data
provider.
No new output layers are created.
**Default menu**: :menuselection:`Vector --> Data Management Tools`
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: Input vector layer (Type: str)

Tool: Define Shapefile projection
Algorithm ID: qgis:definecurrentprojection
Description: Sets the CRS (projection) of an existing Shapefile format dataset to
the provided CRS.
It is very useful when a Shapefile format dataset is missing the
``prj`` file and you know the correct projection.
Contrary to the :ref:`qgisassignprojection` algorithm, it modifies the
current layer and will not output a new layer.
.. note:: For Shapefile datasets, the ``.prj`` and ``.qpj`` files will
   be overwritten - or created if missing - to match the provided CRS.
 :ref:`qgisreprojectlayer`
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: Vector layer with missing projection information (Type: str)
  - CRS: Select the CRS to assign to the vector layer (Type: str)

Tool: Delete duplicate geometries
Algorithm ID: native:deleteduplicategeometries
Description: Finds and removes duplicated geometries.
Attributes are not checked, so in case two features have identical
geometries but different attributes, only one of them will be added to
the result layer.
   :ref:`qgisremovenullgeometries`,
   :ref:`qgisremoveduplicatesbyattribute`
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: The layer with duplicate geometries you want to clean (Type: str)
  - OUTPUT: Specify the output layer. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **layer_output_types** :end-before: **end_layer_output_types** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Create temporary layer]``]

Tool: Delete duplicates by attribute
Algorithm ID: native:removeduplicatesbyattribute
Description: Deletes duplicate rows by only considering the specified field
/ fields.
The first matching row will be retained, and duplicates will be
discarded.
Optionally, these duplicate records can be saved to a separate
output for analysis.
.. seealso:: :ref:`qgisdeleteduplicategeometries`
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: The input layer (Type: str)
  - FIELDS: Fields defining duplicates. Features with identical values for all these fields are considered duplicates. (Type: list)
  - OUTPUT: Specify the output layer containing the unique features. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **layer_output_types** :end-before: **end_layer_output_types** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Create temporary layer]``]

Tool: Detect dataset changes
Algorithm ID: native:detectvectorchanges
Description: Compares two vector layers, and determines which features are
unchanged, added or deleted between the two.
It is designed for comparing two different versions of the same
dataset.
  Detect dataset change example
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - ORIGINAL: The vector layer considered as the original version (Type: str)
  - REVISED: The revised or modified vector layer (Type: str)

Tool: Drop geometries
Algorithm ID: native:dropgeometries
Description: Creates a simple *geometryless* copy of the input layer attribute
table.
It keeps the attribute table of the source layer.
If the file is saved in a local folder, you can choose between many
file formats.
of point, line, and polygon features
   :ref:`qgisremovenullgeometries`
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: The input vector layer (Type: str)
  - OUTPUT: Specify the output geometryless layer. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **layer_output_types_append** :end-before: **end_layer_output_types_append** (Type: str)

Tool: Execute SQL
Algorithm ID: qgis:executesql
Description: Runs a simple or complex query based only on SELECT with ``SQL`` syntax 
on the source layer.
Input datasources are identified with ``input1``, ``input2``... ``inputN`` and
a simple query will look like ``SELECT * FROM input1``.
Beside a simple query, you can add expressions or variables within the 
``SQL query`` parameter itself. This is particulary useful if this algorithm is
executed within a Processing model and you want to use a model input as a
parameter of the query. An example of a query will then be ``SELECT * FROM 
[% @table %]`` where ``@table`` is the variable that identifies the model input.
The result of the query will be added as a new layer.
   :ref:`qgispostgisexecutesql`
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT_DATASOURCES: List of layers to query. In the SQL editor you can refer these layers with their **real** name or also with **input1**, **input2**, **inputN** depending on how many layers have been chosen. (Type: list)
  - INPUT_QUERY: Type the string of your SQL query, e.g. ``SELECT * FROM input1``. (Type: str)
  - OUTPUT: Specify the output layer created by the query. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **layer_output_types** :end-before: **end_layer_output_types** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Create temporary layer]``]

Tool: Export layers to DXF
Algorithm ID: native:dxfexport
Description: Exports layers to DXF file. For each layer, you can choose a field whose values
are used to split features in generated destination layers in DXF output.
.. seealso:: :ref:`create_dxf_files`
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - LAYERS: Input vector layers to export (Type: list)
  - SYMBOLOGY_MODE: Type of symbology to apply to output layers. You can choose between: * 0 --- No Symbology * 1 --- Feature Symbology * 2 --- Symbol Layer Symbology (Type: enum) [Default: 0]
  - SYMBOLOGY_SCALE: Default scale of data export. (Type: str) [Default: 1:1 000 000]
  - ENCODING: Encoding to apply to layers. (Type: enum)
  - CRS: Choose the CRS for the output layer. (Type: str)
  - USE_LAYER_TITLE: Name the output layer with the layer title (as set in QGIS) instead of the layer name. (Type: bool) [Default: False]
  - FORCE_2D: - (Type: bool) [Default: False]
  - MTEXT: Exports labels as MTEXT or TEXT elements (Type: bool) [Default: False]
  - OUTPUT: Specification of the output DXF file. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **file_output_types** :end-before: **end_file_output_types** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Save to temporary file]``]

Tool: Extract selected features
Algorithm ID: native:saveselectedfeatures
Description: Saves the selected features as a new layer.
.. note:: If the selected layer has no selected features, the newly
   created layer will be empty.
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: Layer to save the selection from (Type: str)
  - OUTPUT: Specify the vector layer for the selected features. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **layer_output_types** :end-before: **end_layer_output_types** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Create temporary layer]``]

Tool: Extract Shapefile encoding
Algorithm ID: native:shpencodinginfo
Description: Extracts the attribute encoding information embedded in a Shapefile.
Both the encoding specified by an optional :file:`.cpg` file and
any encoding details present in the :file:`.dbf` LDID header block are considered.
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: ESRI Shapefile (:file:`.SHP`) Layer to extract the encoding information. (Type: str)

Tool: Find projection
Algorithm ID: qgis:findprojection
Description: Creates a shortlist of candidate coordinate reference systems, for
instance for a layer with an unknown projection.
The area that the layer is expected to cover must be specified via the
target area parameter.
The coordinate reference system for this target area must be known to
QGIS.
The algorithm operates by testing the layer's extent in every known
reference system and then listing any for which the bounds would be
near the target area if the layer was in this projection.
   :ref:`qgisdefinecurrentprojection`, :ref:`qgisreprojectlayer`
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: Layer with unknown projection (Type: str)
  - TARGET_AREA: The area that the layer covers. .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **extent_options** :end-before: **end_extent_options** (Type: str)
  - OUTPUT: Specify the table (geometryless layer) for the CRS suggestions (EPSG codes). One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **layer_output_types** :end-before: **end_layer_output_types** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Create temporary layer]``]

Tool: Flatten relationship
Algorithm ID: native:flattenrelationships
Description: Flattens a :ref:`relationship <vector_relations>` for a vector layer,
exporting a single layer containing one parent feature per 
related child feature. This master feature contains all the 
attributes for the related features.
This allows to have the relation as a plain table that can be e.g. exported to CSV.
  Form of a region with related children (left) - A duplicate region feature for each related child, with joined attributes (right)
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: Layer with the relationship that should be de-normalized (Type: str)

Tool: Join attributes by field value
Algorithm ID: native:joinattributestable
Description: Takes an input vector layer and creates a new vector layer that is an
extended version of the input one, with additional attributes in its
attribute table.
The additional attributes and their values are taken from a second
vector layer.
An attribute is selected in each of them to define the join criteria.
   :ref:`qgisjoinattributesbylocation`
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: Input vector layer. The output layer will consist of the features of this layer with attributes from matching features in the second layer. (Type: str)
  - FIELD: Field of the source layer to use for the join (Type: str)
  - INPUT_2: Layer with the attribute table to join (Type: str)
  - FIELD_2: Field of the second (join) layer to use for the join The type of the field must be equal to (or compatible with) the input table field type. (Type: str)
  - METHOD: The type of the final joined layer. One of: * 0 --- Create separate feature for each matching feature (one-to-many) * 1 --- Take attributes of the first matching feature only (one-to-one) (Type: enum) [Default: 1]
  - DISCARD_NONMATCHING: Check if you don't want to keep the features that could not be joined (Type: bool) [Default: True]

Tool: Join attributes by location
Algorithm ID: native:joinattributesbylocation
Description: Takes an input vector layer and creates a new vector layer that is an
extended version of the input one, with additional attributes in its
attribute table.
The additional attributes and their values are taken from a second
vector layer.
A spatial criteria is applied to select the values from the second
layer that are added to each feature from the first layer.
   :ref:`qgisjoinattributestable`, :ref:`qgisjoinbylocationsummary`
Exploring spatial relations

   :end-before: **end_geometric_predicates**

  - INPUT: Input vector layer. The output layer will consist of the features of this layer with attributes from matching features in the second layer. (Type: str)
  - PREDICATE: Type of spatial relation the source feature should have with the target feature so that they could be joined. One or more of: * 0 --- intersect * 1 --- contain * 2 --- equal * 3 --- touch * 4 --- overlap * 5 --- are within * 6 --- cross If more than one condition is chosen, at least one of them (OR operation) has to be met for a feature to be extracted.   - JOIN: The join layer. Features of this vector layer will **add** their attributes to the source layer attribute table if they satisfy the spatial relationship. (Type: str)

  - DISCARD_NONMATCHING: Remove from the output the input layer's features which could not be joined (Type: bool) [Default: False]

Tool: Join attributes by location (summary)
Algorithm ID: qgis:joinbylocationsummary
Description: Takes an input vector layer and creates a new vector layer that is an

The additional attributes and their values are taken from a second

One or more of: * 0 --- intersect * 1 --- contain * 2 --- equal * 3 --- touch * 4 --- overlap * 5 --- are within * 6 --- cross If more than one condition is chosen, at least one of them (OR operation) has to be met for a feature to be extracted. Tool: Join attributes by nearest
Algorithm ID: native:joinbynearest
Description: Takes an input vector layer and creates a new vector
layer with additional fields in its attribute table.
The additional attributes and their values are taken from a second
vector layer.
Features are joined by finding the closest features from each layer.
By default only the nearest feature is joined, but the join can also
join to the k-nearest neighboring features.
If a maximum distance is specified, only features which are closer
than this distance will be matched.
   :ref:`qgisjoinattributestable`,
   :ref:`qgisjoinattributesbylocation`, :ref:`qgisdistancematrix`
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: The input layer. (Type: str)
  - INPUT_2: The join layer. (Type: str)
  - FIELDS_TO_COPY: Join layer fields to copy (if empty, all fields will be copied). (Type: str)
  - DISCARD_NONMATCHING: Remove from the output the input layer records which could not be joined (Type: bool) [Default: False]
  - PREFIX: Joined field prefix (Type: str)
  - NEIGHBORS: Maximum number of nearest neighbors (Type: int) [Default: 1]
  - MAX_DISTANCE: Maximum search distance (Type: float)
  - NON_MATCHING: Specify the vector layer containing the features that could not be joined. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **layer_output_types_skip** :end-before: **end_layer_output_types_skip** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Skip output]``]

Tool: Merge vector layers
Algorithm ID: native:mergevectorlayers
Description: Combines multiple vector layers of the **same geometry** type into a
single one.
The attribute table of the resulting layer will contain the fields from all
input layers. If fields with the same name but different types are found then
the exported field will be automatically converted into a string type field.
New fields storing the original layer name and source are also added.
If any input layers contain Z or M values, then the output layer will
also contain these values.
Similarly, if any of the input layers are multi-part, the output layer
will also be a multi-part layer.
Optionally, the destination coordinate reference system (CRS) for the
merged layer can be set. If it is not set, the CRS will be taken from

Tool: Add geometry attributes
Algorithm ID: qgis:exportaddgeometrycolumns
Description: Computes geometric properties of the features in a vector layer and
includes them in the output layer.
It generates a new vector layer with the same content as the input one,
but with additional attributes, containing geometric measurements
based on a selected CRS.
The attributes added to the table depend on the geometry type and
dimension of the input layer:
* for **point** layers: X (``xcoord``), Y (``ycoord``), Z (``zcoord``)
  coordinates and/or M value (``mvalue``)
* for **line** layers: ``length`` and, for the LineString and
  CompoundCurve geometry types, the feature ``sinuosity`` and straight
  distance (``straightdis``)
* for **polygon** layers: ``perimeter`` and ``area``
**Default menu**: :menuselection:`Vector --> Geometry Tools`

Affine transformations can include translation, scaling and rotation.

Z and M values (if present) can be translated and scaled.

  - SCALE_Z: Scaling value (expansion or contraction) to apply on the Z axis. (Type: int) [Default: 1]

Tool: Aggregate
Algorithm ID: native:aggregate
Description: Takes a vector or table layer and creates a new layer by aggregating
features based on a ``group by`` expression.
Features for which ``group by`` expression returns the same value are
grouped together.
It is possible to group all source features together using constant
value in ``group by`` parameter, example: NULL.
It is also possible to group features by multiple fields using Array
function, example: Array("Field1", "Field2").
Geometries (if present) are combined into one multipart geometry for
each group.
Output attributes are computed depending on each given aggregate
definition.
This algorithm allows to use the default
:ref:`aggregates functions <aggregates_function>` of the QGIS Expression engine.
.. seealso:: :ref:`qgiscollect`, :ref:`qgisdissolve`
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: Input vector layer (Type: str)
  - GROUP_BY: Choose the grouping field. If *NULL* all features will be grouped. (Type: str) [Default: 'NULL']
  - AGGREGATES: List of output layer field definitions. Example of a field definition: *{'aggregate': 'sum', 'delimiter': ',', 'input': ' $area', 'length': 10, 'name': 'totarea', 'precision': 0, 'type': 6}* By default, the list contains all the fields of the input layer. In the GUI, you can edit these fields and their definitions, and you can also: * Click the button to add a new field. * Click to delete the selected field. * Use and to change order of the fields. * Click to reset to the default (the fields of the input layer). For each of the fields you'd like to retrieve information from, you need to define the following: ``Input expression`` [expression] (``input``) Field or expression from the input layer. ``Aggregate function`` [enumeration] (``aggregate``) :ref:`Function <aggregates_function>` to use on the input expression to return the aggregated value. numeric data type) ``Delimiter`` [string] (``delimiter``) Text string to separate aggregated values, for example in case of concatenation. ``Output field name`` [string] (``name``) Name of the aggregated field in the output layer. By default input field name is kept. ``Type`` [enumeration] (``type``) Data type of the output field. One of: * 1 --- Boolean * 2 --- Integer * 4 --- Integer64 * 6 --- Double * 10 --- String * 14 --- Date * 16 --- DateTime ``Length`` [number] (``length``) Length of the output field. ``Precision`` [number] (``precision``) Precision of the output field. (Type: list) [Default: *concatenate* (for string data type), *sum* (for]
  - OUTPUT: Specify the output (aggregate) layer One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **layer_output_types** :end-before: **end_layer_output_types** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Create temporary layer]``]

Description: Returns the closure of the combinatorial boundary of the input

Only for polygon and line layers.
For **polygon geometries** , the boundary consists of all the lines
making up the rings of the polygon.
   Boundaries (black dashed line) of the source polygon layer
For **lines geometries**, the boundaries are their end points.
   Boundary layer (red points) for lines. In yellow a selected feature.

Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: Input line or polygon vector layer (Type: str)
  - OUTPUT: Specify the output (boundary) layer. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **layer_output_types_append** :end-before: **end_layer_output_types_append** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Create temporary layer]``]

Tool: Buffer
Algorithm ID: native:buffer
Description: Computes a buffer area for all the features in an input layer, using
a fixed or data defined distance.
It is possible to use a negative distance for polygon input layers.
In this case the buffer will result in a smaller polygon (setback).
   Buffer (in yellow) of points, line, polygon with positive buffer, 
   and polygon with negative buffer 
:ref:`features in-place modification <processing_inplace_edit>` 
of polygon features
   :ref:`qgismultiringconstantbuffer`, :ref:`qgisbufferbym`
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: Input vector layer (Type: str)
  - DISTANCE: Buffer distance (from the boundary of each feature). You can use the Data Defined button on the right to choose a field from which the radius will be calculated. This way you can have different radius for each feature (see :ref:`qgisvariabledistancebuffer`). (Type: float) [Default: 10.0]
  - SEGMENTS: Controls the number of line segments to use to approximate a quarter circle when creating rounded offsets. (Type: int) [Default: 5]
  - END_CAP_STYLE: Controls how line endings are handled in the buffer. One of: * 0 --- Round * 1 --- Flat * 2 --- Square Round, flat and square cap styles (Type: enum) [Default: 0]
  - JOIN_STYLE: Specifies whether round, miter or beveled joins should be used when offsetting corners in a line. Options are: * 0 --- Round * 1 --- Miter * 2 --- Bevel Round, miter, and bevel join styles (Type: enum) [Default: 0]
  - MITER_LIMIT: Sets the maximum distance from the offset geometry to use when creating a mitered join as a factor of the offset distance (only applicable for miter join styles). Minimum: 1.0 A 10m buffer with a limit of 2 and a 10m buffer with a limit of 1 (Type: float) [Default: 2.0]
  - DISSOLVE: Dissolve the final buffer. If ``True`` (checked), overlapping buffers will be dissolved (combined) into a single multipart feature. Standard (three single part features - left), dissolved (1 multipart feature with 2 parts - right) (Type: bool) [Default: False]
  - OUTPUT: Specify the output (buffer) layer. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **layer_output_types_append** :end-before: **end_layer_output_types_append** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Create temporary layer]``]
Advanced Parameters:
  - SEPARATE_DISJOINT: If ``True`` (checked) and dissolved is checked, features that do not overlap or touch will be exported as separate features (instead of parts of a multipart feature). Results in 2 single part features (Type: bool) [Default: False]

Tool: Centroids
Algorithm ID: native:centroids
Description: Creates a new point layer, with points representing the centroids
of the geometries of the input layer.
The centroid is a single point representing the barycenter (of all
parts) of the feature, so it can be outside the feature borders.
But can also be a point on each part of the feature.
The attributes of the points in the output layer are the same
as for the original features.
   The red stars represent the centroids of the features of the
   input layer.
:ref:`features in-place modification <processing_inplace_edit>`
of point features
.. seealso:: :ref:`qgispointonsurface`
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: Input vector layer (Type: str)
  - ALL_PARTS: If True (checked), a centroid will be created for each part of the geometry (Type: bool) [Default: False]
  - OUTPUT: Specify the output (centroid) layer. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **layer_output_types_append** :end-before: **end_layer_output_types_append** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Create temporary layer]``]

Tool: Check validity
Algorithm ID: qgis:checkvalidity
Description: Performs a validity check on the geometries of a vector layer.
The geometries are classified in three groups (valid, invalid and
error) and for each group, a vector layer with its features is
generated:
* The **Valid output** layer contains only the valid features (without
  topological errors).
* The **Invalid output** layer contains all the invalid features found
  by the algorithm.
* The **Error output** layer is a point layer that points to where the
  invalid features were found.
The attribute tables of the generated layers will contain some
additional information ("message" for the **error** layer, "FID" and
"_errors" for the **invalid** layer and  only "FID" for the **valid**
layer):
The attribute table of each generated vector layer will contain some
additional information (number of errors found and types of error):
   Left: the input layer. Right: the valid layer (green), the invalid
   layer (orange)
   :ref:`geometry_checker`
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT_LAYER: Input vector layer (Type: str)
  - METHOD: Method to use to check validity. Options: * 0: The one selected in digitizing settings * 1: QGIS * 2: GEOS (Type: enum) [Default: 2]
  - IGNORE_RING_SELF_INTERSECTION: Ignore self intersecting rings when checking for validity. (Type: bool) [Default: False]
  - INVALID_OUTPUT: Vector layer containing copy of the invalid features of the source layer with the field ``_errors`` listing the summary of the error(s) found. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **layer_output_types_skip** :end-before: **end_layer_output_types_skip** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Create temporary layer]``]
  - ERROR_OUTPUT: Point layer of the exact position of the validity problems detected with the ``message`` field describing the error(s) found. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **layer_output_types_skip** :end-before: **end_layer_output_types_skip** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Create temporary layer]``]

Tool: Collect geometries
Algorithm ID: native:collect
Description: Takes a vector layer and collects its geometries into new multipart
geometries.
One or more attributes can be specified to collect only geometries
belonging to the same class (having the same value for the specified
attributes), alternatively all geometries can be collected.
All output geometries will be converted to multi geometries, even
those with just a single part.
This algorithm does not dissolve overlapping geometries - they will
be collected together without modifying the shape of each geometry
part.
See the 'Promote to multipart' or 'Aggregate' algorithms for
alternative options.
   :ref:`qgisdissolve`
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: Input vector layer (Type: str)
  - FIELD: Choose one or more attributes to collect the geometries (Type: list)
  - OUTPUT: Vector layer with collected geometries (Type: str)

  - INPUT: Input line or polygon vector layer (Type: str)
  - VERTICES: Number of vertices to add to each segment (Type: int) [Default: 1]
  - OUTPUT: Specify the output vector layer. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **layer_output_types_append** :end-before: **end_layer_output_types_append** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Create temporary layer]``]

Tool: Densify by interval
Algorithm ID: native:densifygeometriesgivenaninterval
Description: Takes a polygon or line layer and generates a new one in which the
geometries have a larger number of vertices than the original one.
The geometries are densified by adding regularly placed extra
vertices inside each segment so that the maximum distance between
any two vertices does not exceed the specified distance.
If the geometries have Z or M values present then these will be
linearly interpolated at the added vertices.
**Example**
Specifying a distance of 3 would cause the segment
``[0 0] -> [10 0]`` to be converted to
``[0 0] -> [2.5 0] -> [5 0] -> [7.5 0] -> [10 0]``,
since 3 extra vertices are required on the segment and spacing these
at 2.5 increments allows them to be evenly spaced over the segment.
   Densify geometry at a given interval
:ref:`features in-place modification <processing_inplace_edit>`
of line and polygon features
.. seealso:: :ref:`qgisdensifygeometries`
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: Input line or polygon vector layer (Type: str)
  - INTERVAL: Maximum distance between two consecutive vertices (Type: float) [Default: 1.0]
  - OUTPUT: Specify the output vector layer. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **layer_output_types_append** :end-before: **end_layer_output_types_append** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Create temporary layer]``]

Tool: Dissolve
Algorithm ID: native:dissolve
Description: Takes a vector layer and combines its features into new features.
One or more attributes can be specified to dissolve features
belonging to the same class (having the same value for the specified
attributes), alternatively all features can be dissolved to a single
feature.
All output geometries will be converted to multi geometries.
In case the input is a polygon layer, common boundaries of adjacent
polygons being dissolved will get erased.
If enabled, the optional "Keep disjoint features separate" setting will
cause features and parts that do not overlap or touch to be exported as 
separate features (instead of parts of a single multipart feature).
The resulting attribute table will have the same fields as the input
layer.
The values in the output layer's fields are the ones of the first
input feature that happens to be processed.
   Dissolving a layer into a single multipart feature
.. seealso:: :ref:`qgisaggregate`, :ref:`qgiscollect`
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: Input vector layer (Type: str)
  - OUTPUT: Specify the output vector layer. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **layer_output_types** :end-before: **end_layer_output_types** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Create temporary layer]``]
Advanced Parameters:
  - SEPARATE_DISJOINT: Parts of dissolved features are exported as separate features (instead of parts of a multipart feature). source (left), dissolve all (3 distinct features - right) source (left), dissolve on field (5 distinct features - right) (Type: bool) [Default: False]

Tool: Drape (set Z value from raster)
Algorithm ID: native:setzfromraster
Description: Uses values sampled from a band within a raster layer to set the Z
value for every overlapping vertex in the feature geometry.
The raster values can optionally be scaled by a preset amount.
If Z values already exist in the layer, they will be overwritten with
the new value.
If no Z values exist, the geometry will be upgraded to include the Z
dimension.
:ref:`features in-place modification <processing_inplace_edit>`
of point, line, and polygon features with Z enabled
.. seealso:: :ref:`qgissetmfromraster`, :ref:`qgissetzvalue`
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: Input vector layer (Type: str)
  - RASTER: Raster layer with Z values (Type: str)
  - BAND: The raster band to take the Z values from (Type: str) [Default: 1]
  - NODATA: Value to use in case the vertex does not intersect (a valid pixel of) the raster (Type: int) [Default: 0]
  - SCALE: Scaling value: the band values are multiplied by this value. (Type: float) [Default: 1.0]
  - OFFSET: Offset value: it is algebraically added to the band values after applying the "Scale factor". (Type: float) [Default: 0.0]
  - OUTPUT: Specify the output vector layer (with Z values from the raster layer). One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **layer_output_types_append** :end-before: **end_layer_output_types_append** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Create temporary layer]``]

Tool: Z values
Algorithm ID: native:dropmzvalues
Description: Removes M (measure) or Z (altitude) values from input geometries.
.. seealso:: :ref:`qgissetmvalue`, :ref:`qgissetzvalue`
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: Input vector layer with M or Z values (Type: str)
  - DROP_M_VALUES: Removes the M values from the geometries (Type: bool) [Default: False]
  - DROP_Z_VALUES: Removes the Z values from the geometries (Type: bool) [Default: False]
  - OUTPUT: Specify the output vector layer. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **layer_output_types_append** :end-before: **end_layer_output_types_append** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Create temporary layer]``]

Tool: Eliminate selected polygons
Algorithm ID: qgis:eliminateselectedpolygons
Description: Combines selected polygons of the input layer with certain adjacent
polygons by erasing their common boundary.
The adjacent polygon can be either the one with the largest or
smallest area or the one sharing the largest common boundary with the
polygon to be eliminated.
Eliminate is normally used to get rid of sliver polygons, i.e. tiny
polygons that are a result of polygon intersection processes where
boundaries of the inputs are similar but not identical.
.. seealso:: :ref:`qgisfixgeometries`
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: Input polygon vector layer (Type: str)
  - MODE: Choose the parameter to use in order to get rid of the selected polygons: * 0 --- Largest Area * 1 --- Smallest Area * 2 --- Largest Common Boundary (Type: enum) [Default: None]
  - OUTPUT: Specify the output vector layer. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **layer_output_types** :end-before: **end_layer_output_types** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Create temporary layer]``]

Tool: Explode lines
Algorithm ID: native:explodelines
Description: Takes a lines layer and creates a new one in which each line layer is
replaced by a set of lines representing the segments in the original
line.
Each line in the resulting layer contains only a start and an end
point, with no intermediate vertices between them.
   The original line layer and the exploded one
:ref:`features in-place modification <processing_inplace_edit>`
of line features
.. seealso:: :ref:`qgissubdivide`, :ref:`qgislinesubstring`
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: Input line vector layer (Type: str)
  - OUTPUT: Specify the output vector layer. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **layer_output_types_append** :end-before: **end_layer_output_types_append** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Create temporary layer]``]

Tool: Extend lines
Algorithm ID: native:extendlines
Description: Extends line geometry by a specified amount at the start and end of
the line.
Lines are extended using the bearing of the first and last segment in
the line.
   The red dashes represent the initial and final extension of the
   original layer
:ref:`features in-place modification <processing_inplace_edit>`
of line features
.. seealso:: :ref:`qgislinesubstring`
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: Input line vector layer (Type: str)
  - START_DISTANCE: Distance by which to extend the first segment of the line (starting point) (Type: float)
  - END_DISTANCE: Distance by which to extend the last segment of the line (ending point) (Type: float)
  - OUTPUT: Specify the output vector layer. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **layer_output_types_append** :end-before: **end_layer_output_types_append** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Create temporary layer]``]

Tool: Extract M values
Algorithm ID: native:extractmvalues
Description: Extracts M values from geometries into feature attributes.
By default only the M value from the first vertex of each feature is
extracted, however the algorithm can optionally calculate statistics
on all of the geometry's M values, including sum, mean, minimum and
maximum.
.. seealso:: :ref:`qgisextractzvalues`, :ref:`qgissetmvalue`, :ref:`qgisdropmzvalues`
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: Input vector layer (Type: str)
  - SUMMARIES: Statistics on the M values of a geometry. One or more of: * 0 --- First * 1 --- Last * 2 --- Count * 3 --- Sum * 4 --- Mean * 5 --- Median * 6 --- St.dev (pop) * 7 --- Minimum * 8 --- Maximum * 9 --- Range * 10 --- Minority * 11 --- Majority * 12 --- Variety * 13 --- Q1 * 14 --- Q3 * 15 --- IQR (Type: enum) [Default: [0]]
  - COLUMN_PREFIX: The prefix for the output (M) column (Type: str) [Default: 'm\_']
  - OUTPUT: Specify the output layer. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **layer_output_types_append** :end-before: **end_layer_output_types_append** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Create temporary layer]``]

Tool: Extract specific vertices
Algorithm ID: native:extractspecificvertices
Description: Takes a vector layer and generates a point layer with points
representing specific vertices in the input geometries.
For instance, this algorithm can be used to extract the first or last
vertices in the geometry.
The attributes associated to each point are the same ones associated
to the feature that the vertex belongs to.
The vertex indices parameter accepts a comma separated string
specifying the indices of the vertices to extract.
The first vertex corresponds to an index of 0, the second vertex has
an index of 1, etc. Negative indices can be used to find vertices at
the end of the geometry, e.g., an index of -1 corresponds to the last
vertex, -2 corresponds to the second last vertex, etc.
Additional fields are added to the vertices indicating the specific
vertex position (e.g., 0, -1, etc), the original vertex index, the
vertex’s part and its index within the part (as well as its ring for
polygons), distance along the original geometry and bisector angle of
vertex for the original geometry.
:ref:`features in-place modification <processing_inplace_edit>`
of point features
   :ref:`qgisfilterverticesbyz`
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: Input vector layer (Type: str)
  - VERTICES: Comma-separated string of the indices of the vertices to extract. (Type: str) [Default: '0']
  - OUTPUT: Specify the output vector layer. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **layer_output_types_append** :end-before: **end_layer_output_types_append** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Create temporary layer]``]

Tool: Extract vertices
Algorithm ID: native:extractvertices
Description: Takes a vector layer and generates a point layer with points
representing the vertices in the input geometries.
The attributes associated to each point are the same ones associated
to the feature that the vertex belongs to.
Additional fields are added to the vertices indicating the vertex
index (beginning at 0), the feature’s part and its index within the
part (as well as its ring for polygons), distance along original
geometry and bisector angle of vertex for original geometry.
   Vertices extracted for line and polygon layer
:ref:`features in-place modification <processing_inplace_edit>`
of point features
   :ref:`qgisfilterverticesbym`, :ref:`qgisfilterverticesbyz`
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: Input vector layer (Type: str)
  - OUTPUT: Specify the output vector layer. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **layer_output_types_append** :end-before: **end_layer_output_types_append** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Create temporary layer]``]

Tool: Extract Z values
Algorithm ID: native:extractzvalues
Description: Extracts Z values from geometries into feature attributes.
By default only the Z value from the first vertex of each feature is
extracted, however the algorithm can optionally calculate statistics
on all of the geometry's Z values, including sum, mean, minimum and
maximum.
   :ref:`qgisdropmzvalues`
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: Input vector layer (Type: str)
  - SUMMARIES: Statistics on the Z values of a geometry. One or more of: * 0 --- First * 1 --- Last * 2 --- Count * 3 --- Sum * 4 --- Mean * 5 --- Median * 6 --- St.dev (pop) * 7 --- Minimum * 8 --- Maximum * 9 --- Range * 10 --- Minority * 11 --- Majority * 12 --- Variety * 13 --- Q1 * 14 --- Q3 * 15 --- IQR (Type: enum) [Default: [0]]
  - COLUMN_PREFIX: The prefix for the output (Z) column (Type: str) [Default: 'z\_']
  - OUTPUT: Specify the output layer. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **layer_output_types_append** :end-before: **end_layer_output_types_append** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Create temporary layer]``]

Tool: Filter vertices by M value
Algorithm ID: native:filterverticesbym
Description: Filters away vertices based on their M value, returning geometries
with only vertex points that have a M value greater than or equal to
the specified minimum value and/or less than or equal to the maximum
value.
If the minimum value is not specified then only the maximum value is
tested, and similarly if the maximum value is not specified then only
the minimum value is tested.
   The red line represents the black line with only vertices whose M
   value is <=10.
:ref:`features in-place modification <processing_inplace_edit>`
of line and polygon features with M enabled
.. note:: Depending on the input geometry attributes and the filters
   used, the resultant geometries created by this algorithm may no
   longer be valid.
 :ref:`qgisextractspecificvertices`
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: Input line or polygon vector layer to remove vertices from (Type: str)
  - OUTPUT: Specify the output vector layer. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **layer_output_types_append** :end-before: **end_layer_output_types_append** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Create temporary layer]``]

Tool: Filter vertices by Z value
Algorithm ID: native:filterverticesbyz
Description: Filters away vertices based on their Z value, returning geometries
with only vertex points that have a Z value greater than or equal to
the specified minimum value and/or less than or equal to the maximum
value.
If the minimum value is not specified then only the maximum value is
tested, and similarly if the maximum value is not specified then only
the minimum value is tested.
   The red line represents the black line with only vertices whose Z
   value is <=10.
:ref:`features in-place modification <processing_inplace_edit>`
of line and polygon features with Z enabled
.. note:: Depending on the input geometry attributes and the filters
   used, the resultant geometries created by this algorithm may no
   longer be valid.
   You may need to run the :ref:`qgisfixgeometries` algorithm to
   ensure their validity.
 :ref:`qgisextractspecificvertices`
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: Input line or polygon vector layer to remove vertices from (Type: str)
  - OUTPUT: Specify the output vector layer. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **layer_output_types_append** :end-before: **end_layer_output_types_append** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Create temporary layer]``]

Tool: Fix geometries
Algorithm ID: native:fixgeometries
Description: Attempts to create a valid representation of a given invalid geometry
without losing any of the input vertices.
Already valid geometries are returned without further intervention.
Always outputs multi-geometry layer.
:ref:`features in-place modification <processing_inplace_edit>`
of point, line, and polygon features without M enabled
.. note:: M values will be dropped from the output.
.. seealso:: :ref:`qgischeckvalidity`
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: Input vector layer (Type: str)
  - METHOD: Method used to repair the geometries. One of: * 0 --- ``Linework``: combines all rings into a set of noded lines and then extracts valid polygons from that linework * 1 --- ``Structure``: first makes all rings valid and then merges shells and subtracts holes from shells to generate valid result. Assumes that holes and shells are correctly categorized. Requires QGIS version built with GEOS 3.10 or later (check :menuselection:`Help --> About` menu). (Type: enum) [Default: 1]
  - OUTPUT: Specify the output vector layer. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **layer_output_types_append** :end-before: **end_layer_output_types_append** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Create temporary layer]``]

Tool: rule
Algorithm ID: native:forcerhr
Description: Forces polygon geometries to respect the Right-Hand-Rule, in which
the area that is bounded by a polygon is to the right of the boundary.
In particular, the exterior ring is oriented in a clockwise
direction and any interior rings in a counter-clockwise direction.
:ref:`features in-place modification <processing_inplace_edit>`
of polygon features
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: Input vector layer (Type: str)
  - OUTPUT: Specify the output vector layer. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **layer_output_types_append** :end-before: **end_layer_output_types_append** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Create temporary layer]``]

Tool: Geodesic line split at antimeridian
Algorithm ID: native:antimeridiansplit
Description: Splits a line into multiple geodesic segments, whenever
the line crosses the antimeridian (±180 degrees longitude).
Splitting at the antimeridian helps the visual display of the lines in
some projections.
The returned geometry will always be a multi-part geometry.
Whenever line segments in the input geometry cross the antimeridian,
they will be split into two segments, with the latitude of the
breakpoint being determined using a geodesic line connecting the
points either side of this segment.
The current project ellipsoid setting will be used when calculating
this breakpoint.
If the input geometry contains M or Z values, these will be linearly
interpolated for the new vertices created at the antimeridian.
:ref:`features in-place modification <processing_inplace_edit>`
of line features
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: Input line vector layer (Type: str)
  - OUTPUT: Specify the output line vector layer. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **layer_output_types_append** :end-before: **end_layer_output_types_append** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Create temporary layer]``]

Tool: Geometry by expression
Algorithm ID: native:geometrybyexpression
Description: Updates existing geometries (or creates new geometries) for input
features by use of a QGIS expression.
This allows complex geometry modifications which can utilize all the
flexibility of the QGIS expression engine to manipulate and create
geometries for output features.
For help with QGIS expression functions, see the inbuilt help available
in the :ref:`expression builder <vector_expressions>`.
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: Input vector layer (Type: str)
  - OUTPUT_GEOMETRY: The output geometry strongly depends on the expression: for instance, if you create a buffer the geometry type has to be polygon. One of: * 0 --- Polygon * 1 --- Line * 2 --- Point (Type: enum) [Default: 0]
  - WITH_Z: Choose if the output geometry should include the Z dimension (Type: bool) [Default: False]
  - WITH_M: Choose if the output geometry should include the M dimension (Type: bool) [Default: False]
  - EXPRESSION: Add the geometry expression you want to use. You can use the button to open the Expression Dialog. The dialog lists all the relevant expressions, together with their help and guide. (Type: str) [Default: '$geometry']
  - OUTPUT: Specify the output vector layer. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **layer_output_types_append** :end-before: **end_layer_output_types_append** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Create temporary layer]``]

Tool: Interpolate point on line
Algorithm ID: native:interpolatepoint
Description: Creates a point geometry interpolated at a set distance along line or
curve geometries.
Z and M values are linearly interpolated from existing values.
If a multipart geometry is encountered, only the first part is
considered when calculating the substring.
If the specified distance is greater than the input feature's length,
the resultant feature will have a null geometry.
   Interpolated point at 500m of the beginning of the line
.. seealso:: :ref:`qgispointsalonglines`
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: Input line or polygon vector layer (Type: str)
  - DISTANCE: Distance from the beginning of the line (Type: float) [Default: 0.0]
  - OUTPUT: Specify the output vector layer. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **layer_output_types_append** :end-before: **end_layer_output_types_append** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Create temporary layer]``]

Tool: Keep N biggest parts
Algorithm ID: qgis:keepnbiggestparts
Description: Takes a layer with polygons or multipolygons and returns a new layer
in which only the *n* largest polygons of each multipolygon feature
are kept.
If a feature has *n* or fewer parts, the feature will just be copied.
   Clockwise from top left: original multipart feature, one, two and
   three biggest parts kept
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: Input polygon vector layer (Type: str)
  - PARTS: Number of parts to keep. If 1, only the biggest part of the feature will be kept. (Type: int) [Default: 1]
  - OUTPUT: Specify the output polygon vector layer. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **layer_output_types** :end-before: **end_layer_output_types** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Create temporary layer]``]

Tool: Line substring
Algorithm ID: native:linesubstring
Description: Returns the portion of a line (or curve) which falls between the
specified start and end distances (measured from the beginning of the
line).
Z and M values are linearly interpolated from existing values.
If a multipart geometry is encountered, only the first part is
considered when calculating the substring.
   Substring line with starting distance set at 0 meters and the
   ending distance at 250 meters.
of line features
.. seealso:: :ref:`qgisextendlines`
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: Input line vector layer (Type: str)
  - START_DISTANCE: Distance along the input line to the start point of the output feature (Type: float)
  - END_DISTANCE: Distance along the input line to the end point of the output feature (Type: float)
  - OUTPUT: Specify the output line vector layer. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **layer_output_types_append** :end-before: **end_layer_output_types_append** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Create temporary layer]``]

Tool: Lines to polygons
Algorithm ID: qgis:linestopolygons
Description: Generates a polygon layer using as polygon rings the lines from an
input line layer.
The attribute table of the output layer is the same as the one of
the input layer.
.. seealso:: :ref:`qgispolygonstolines`, :ref:`qgispolygonize`, :ref:`qgisconvertgeometrytype`
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: Input line vector layer (Type: str)
  - OUTPUT: Specify the output polygon vector layer. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **layer_output_types_append** :end-before: **end_layer_output_types_append** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Create temporary layer]``]

Tool: Merge lines
Algorithm ID: native:mergelines
Description: Joins all connected parts of MultiLineString geometries into single
LineString geometries.
If any parts of the input MultiLineString geometries are not
connected, the resultant geometry will be a MultiLineString containing
any lines which could be merged and any non-connected line parts.
:ref:`features in-place modification <processing_inplace_edit>`
of line features
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: Input line vector layer (Type: str)
  - OUTPUT: Specify the output line vector layer. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **layer_output_types_append** :end-before: **end_layer_output_types_append** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Create temporary layer]``]

Tool: Minimum bounding geometry
Algorithm ID: qgis:minimumboundinggeometry
Description: Creates geometries which enclose the features from an input layer.
The features can be grouped by a field.
The output layer will then contain one feature per group value with
a geometry (MBB) that covers the geometries of the features with
matching value.
The following enclosing geometry types are supported:
* bounding box (envelope)
* oriented rectangle
* circle
* convex hull
    Clockwise from top left: envelope, oriented rectangle,
    circle, convex hull
.. seealso:: :ref:`qgisminimumenclosingcircle`
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: Input vector layer (Type: str)
  - TYPE: Enclosing geometry types. One of: * 0 --- Envelope (Bounding Box) * 1 --- Minimum Oriented Rectangle * 2 --- Minimum Enclosing Circle * 3 --- Convex Hull (Type: enum) [Default: 0]
  - OUTPUT: Specify the output polygon vector layer. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **layer_output_types** :end-before: **end_layer_output_types** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Create temporary layer]``]

Tool: Minimum enclosing circles
Algorithm ID: native:minimumenclosingcircle
Description: Calculates the minimum enclosing circles of the features in the input
layer.
   Enclosing circles for each feature
:ref:`features in-place modification <processing_inplace_edit>`
of polygon features
.. seealso:: :ref:`qgisminimumboundinggeometry`
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: Input vector layer (Type: str)
  - SEGMENTS: The number of segments used to approximate a circle. Minimum 8, maximum 100000. (Type: int) [Default: 72]
  - OUTPUT: Specify the output polygon vector layer. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **layer_output_types_append** :end-before: **end_layer_output_types_append** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Create temporary layer]``]

Tool: ring buffer (constant distance)
Algorithm ID: native:multiringconstantbuffer
Description: Computes multi-ring (*donut*) buffer for the features of the
input layer, using a fixed or dynamic distance and number of rings.
   Multi-ring buffer for a line, point and polygon layer
:ref:`features in-place modification <processing_inplace_edit>`
of polygon features
   :ref:`qgisvariabledistancebuffer`,
   :ref:`qgisrectanglesovalsdiamonds`,
   :ref:`qgissinglesidedbuffer`
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: Input vector layer (Type: str)
  - RINGS: The number of rings. It can be a unique value (same number of rings for all the features) or it can be taken from features data (the number of rings depends on feature values). (Type: int) [Default: 1]
  - DISTANCE: Distance between the rings. It can be a unique value (same distance for all the features) or it can be taken from features data (the distance depends on feature values). (Type: float) [Default: 1.0]
  - OUTPUT: Specify the output polygon vector layer. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **layer_output_types_append** :end-before: **end_layer_output_types_append** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Create temporary layer]``]

Tool: Multipart to singleparts
Algorithm ID: native:multiparttosingleparts
Description: Splits multipart features in the input layer into singlepart
features.
The attributes of the output layer are the same as the original ones
but divided into single features.
   Left the multipart source layer and right the single part output
   result
:ref:`features in-place modification <processing_inplace_edit>`
of point, line, and polygon features
.. seealso:: :ref:`qgiscollect`, :ref:`qgispromotetomulti`
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: Input vector layer (Type: str)
  - OUTPUT: Specify the output polygon vector layer. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **layer_output_types_append** :end-before: **end_layer_output_types_append** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Create temporary layer]``]

Tool: Offset lines
Algorithm ID: native:offsetline
Description: Offsets lines by a specified distance.
Positive distances will offset lines to the left, and negative
distances will offset them to the right.
   In blue the source layer, in red the offset one
:ref:`features in-place modification <processing_inplace_edit>`
of line features
.. seealso:: :ref:`qgisarrayoffsetlines`, :ref:`qgistranslategeometry`
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: Input line vector layer (Type: str)
  - DISTANCE: Offset distance. You can use the Data Defined button on the right to choose a field from which the radius will be calculated. This way you can have different radius for each feature (see :ref:`qgisvariabledistancebuffer`). (Type: float) [Default: 10.0]
  - SEGMENTS: Controls the number of line segments to use to approximate a quarter circle when creating rounded offsets. (Type: int) [Default: 8]
  - JOIN_STYLE: Specifies whether round, miter or beveled joins should be used when offsetting corners in a line. Options are: * 0 --- Round * 1 --- Miter * 2 --- Bevel Round, miter, and bevel join styles (Type: enum) [Default: 0]
  - MITER_LIMIT: Sets the maximum distance from the offset geometry to use when creating a mitered join as a factor of the offset distance (only applicable for miter join styles). Minimum: 1.0 A 10m buffer with a limit of 2 and a 10m buffer with a limit of 1 (Type: float) [Default: 2.0]
  - OUTPUT: Specify the output (offset) layer. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **layer_output_types_append** :end-before: **end_layer_output_types_append** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Create temporary layer]``]

Tool: Oriented minimum bounding box
Algorithm ID: native:orientedminimumboundingbox
Description: Calculates the minimum area rotated rectangle for each feature in the
input layer.
   Oriented minimum bounding box
:ref:`features in-place modification <processing_inplace_edit>`
of polygon features
.. seealso:: :ref:`qgisminimumboundinggeometry`
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: Input vector layer (Type: str)
  - OUTPUT: Specify the output polygon vector layer. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **layer_output_types_append** :end-before: **end_layer_output_types_append** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Create temporary layer]``]

Tool: Orthogonalize
Algorithm ID: native:orthogonalize
Description: Attempts to orthogonalize the geometries of the input line or polygon
layer.
This process shifts the vertices in the geometries to try to make
every angle in the geometry either a right angle or a straight line.
   In blue the source layer and in the red orthogonalized
   result
:ref:`features in-place modification <processing_inplace_edit>`
of line and polygon features
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: Input line or polygon vector layer (Type: str)
  - ANGLE_TOLERANCE: Specify the maximum deviation from a right angle or straight line a vertex can have for it to be adjusted. Smaller tolerances mean that only vertices which are already closer to right angles will be adjusted, and larger tolerances mean that vertices which deviate further from right angles will also be adjusted. (Type: int) [Default: 15]
  - MAX_ITERATIONS: Setting a larger number for the maximum number of iterations will result in a more orthogonal geometry at the cost of extra processing time. (Type: int) [Default: 1000]
  - OUTPUT: Specify the output polygon vector layer. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **layer_output_types_append** :end-before: **end_layer_output_types_append** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Create temporary layer]``]

Tool: Point on Surface
Algorithm ID: native:pointonsurface
Description: For each feature of the input layer, returns a point that is
guaranteed to lie on the surface of the feature geometry.
:ref:`features in-place modification <processing_inplace_edit>`
of point features
.. seealso:: :ref:`qgiscentroids`
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: Input vector layer (Type: str)
  - ANGLE_TOLERANCE: If checked, a point will be created for each part of the geometry. (Type: bool)
  - OUTPUT: Specify the output point vector layer. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **layer_output_types_append** :end-before: **end_layer_output_types_append** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Create temporary layer]``]

Tool: Points along geometry
Algorithm ID: native:pointsalonglines
Description: Creates points at regular intervals along line or polygon geometries.
Created points will have new attributes added for the distance along
the geometry and the angle of the line at the point.
An optional start and end offset can be specified, which controls how
far from the start and end of the geometry the points should be
created.
   Points created along the source line layer
.. seealso:: :ref:`qgisinterpolatepoint`
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: Input line or polygon vector layer (Type: str)
  - DISTANCE: Distance between two consecutive points along the line (Type: float) [Default: 1.0]
  - START_OFFSET: Distance from the beginning of the input line, representing the position of the first point. (Type: float) [Default: 0.0]
  - END_OFFSET: Distance from the end of the input line, representing the position beyond which no point feature shoud be created. (Type: float) [Default: 0.0]
  - OUTPUT: Specify the output vector layer. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **layer_output_types_append** :end-before: **end_layer_output_types_append** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Create temporary layer]``]

Tool: Points displacement
Algorithm ID: qgis:pointsdisplacement
Description: Given a distance of proximity, identifies nearby point features and
radially distributes them over a circle whose center represents their
barycenter.
A convenient tool to scatter overlaid features.
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: Input point vector layer (Type: str)
  - PROXIMITY: Distance below which point features are considered close. Close features are distributed altogether. (Type: float) [Default: 1.0]
  - DISTANCE: Radius of the circle on which close features are placed (Type: float) [Default: 1.0]
  - HORIZONTAL: When only two points are identified as close, aligns them horizontally on the circle instead of vertically. (Type: bool) [Default: False]
  - OUTPUT: Specify the output vector layer. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **layer_output_types** :end-before: **end_layer_output_types** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Create temporary layer]``]

Tool: Pole of inaccessibility
Algorithm ID: native:poleofinaccessibility
Description: Calculates the pole of inaccessibility for a polygon layer, which is
the most distant internal point from the boundary of the surface.
This algorithm uses the 'polylabel' algorithm (Vladimir Agafonkin,
2016), which is an iterative approach guaranteed to find the true pole
of inaccessibility within a specified tolerance.
A more precise tolerance (lower value) requires more iterations and
will take longer to calculate.
The distance from the calculated pole to the polygon boundary will be
stored as a new attribute in the output layer.
   Pole of inaccessibility
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: Input vector layer (Type: str)
  - TOLERANCE: Set the tolerance for the calculation (Type: float) [Default: 1.0]
  - OUTPUT: Specify the output polygon vector layer. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **layer_output_types_append** :end-before: **end_layer_output_types_append** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Create temporary layer]``]

Tool: Polygonize
Algorithm ID: native:polygonize
Description: Creates a polygon layer whose features boundaries are generated from a
line layer of **closed** features.
   The yellow polygons generated from the closed lines
.. note:: The line layer must have closed shapes in order to be
   transformed into a polygon.
.. seealso:: :ref:`qgispolygonstolines`, :ref:`qgislinestopolygons`, :ref:`qgisconvertgeometrytype`

Basic Parameters:

  - OUTPUT: Specify the output polygon vector layer. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **layer_output_types** :end-before: **end_layer_output_types** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Create temporary layer]``]

Tool: Polygons to lines
Algorithm ID: native:polygonstolines
Description: Takes a polygon layer and creates a line layer, with lines
representing the boundaries of the polygons in the input layer.
The attribute table of the output layer is the same as the one of
the input layer.
   Black lines as the result of the algorithm
.. seealso:: :ref:`qgislinestopolygons`, :ref:`qgispolygonize`, :ref:`qgisconvertgeometrytype`
Parameters:
Basic Parameters:
  - INPUT: Input polygon vector layer (Type: str)
  - OUTPUT: Specify the output line vector layer. One of: .. include:: ../algs_include.rst :start-after: **layer_output_types_append** :end-before: **end_layer_output_types_append** (Type: str) [Default: ``[Create temporary layer]``]

Tool: Project points (Cartesian)
Algorithm ID: native:projectpointcartesian
Description: Projects point geometries by a specified distance and bearing (azimuth).
:ref:`features in-place modification <processing_inplace_edit>`
of point features
